senses.title: A solution holding all it can
senses.definition: describing a liquid that contains as much dissolved solid as it can hold at that temperature
senses.definitionCN: 指液体在该温度下已含有尽可能多的溶解固体
senses.example: The solution is saturated at this temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个温度下溶液已经饱和。
senses.why: saturated is the participle of saturate, from satur 'full', so it describes a vessel that is full rather than a liquid that is strong.
senses.whyCN: saturated 是 saturate 的分词，出自 satur「满的」，描述的是装满的容器，而不是浓烈的液体。

senses.title: Fat with no double bonds
senses.definition: describing a fat whose fatty acid chains have no double bonds, so every carbon is bonded to as much hydrogen as it can take
senses.definitionCN: 指脂肪酸链没有双键、每个碳都已连上尽可能多氢的脂肪
senses.example: Butter contains a high proportion of saturated fat.
senses.exampleCN: 黄油含有高比例的饱和脂肪。
senses.why: the chemical meaning of saturated is literal: the carbon chain is full of hydrogen, so it can take no more.
senses.whyCN: saturated 的化学义是字面义的：碳链已被氢填满，再接纳不了更多。

senses.title: Soaked through with water
senses.definition: holding as much water as the material can absorb, so that any more runs off or pools
senses.definitionCN: 材料已含尽可能多的水，再多只能流走或积起来
senses.example: His coat was saturated after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后他的外套湿透了。
senses.why: this is the everyday physical sense: cloth, soil and paper are vessels that fill up.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的实体义：布、土壤与纸都是会被填满的容器。

senses.title: Colour at full intensity
senses.definition: describing a colour that is vivid and pure rather than greyed or washed out
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色鲜艳纯正，而非发灰或被冲淡
senses.example: The poster used saturated reds and blues.
senses.exampleCN: 这张海报用了浓艳的红色与蓝色。
senses.why: a hue is saturated when it holds as much pigment as it can, the same fullness applied to light.
senses.whyCN: 色相在容纳尽可能多色素时就是饱和的，这是同一种「满」被用在光上。

senses.title: A market with no room left
senses.definition: describing a market in which every likely buyer has been reached and further growth is hard
senses.definitionCN: 指每个可能的买主都已被触及、进一步增长困难的市场
senses.example: The market for basic phones is saturated.
senses.exampleCN: 基础手机的市场已经饱和。
senses.why: demand is a container, and a saturated market is one that no new product can fill further.
senses.whyCN: 需求是一个容器，饱和的市场就是新产品再也填不进去的市场。

senses.title: A magnet at its limit
senses.definition: describing a magnetic material that cannot be magnetized more strongly by any increase in current
senses.definitionCN: 指无论电流怎样增加都无法磁得更强的磁材料
senses.example: The transformer core became saturated.
senses.exampleCN: 变压器铁芯进入了饱和状态。
senses.why: magnetic capacity fills up like a vessel, after which more current produces no more magnetization.
senses.whyCN: 磁容量像容器一样被填满，此后电流再增加也不产生更多磁性。

senses.title: A compound with only single bonds
senses.titleCN: 饱和化合物的（全为单键）
senses.definition: describing an organic compound whose carbon atoms are joined by single bonds only, with no double or triple bonds
senses.definitionCN: 指碳原子之间只有单键、没有双键或三键的有机化合物
senses.example: The chemists compared saturated and unsaturated oils.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家比较了饱和油与不饱和油。
senses.why: in organic chemistry saturation is a count of bonds: a chain with only single bonds is full of hydrogen.
senses.whyCN: 在有机化学中，饱和是对键的计数：只有单键的链已被氢填满。

senses.title: A life filled with no room
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：被填满而无余地
senses.definition: used figuratively of a schedule, mind or life so full that nothing more can be taken on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指日程、头脑或生活满到再也承担不了新东西
senses.example: His schedule was saturated with meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 他的日程被会议塞得满满的。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the vessel and simply substitutes obligations for water.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留容器，只把水换成了义务。

intro.en: Saturated is the past participle of saturate, from Latin saturare 'to fill, satisfy', from satur 'full', from satis 'enough'. The chemical use for fats and solutions dates from the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: saturated 是 saturate 的过去分词，出自拉丁 saturare「填满、使满足」，再上溯 satur「满的」与 satis「足够」。用于脂肪与溶液的化学义始于十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Satis meant 'enough'; its deeper origin is reconstructed as a root of satisfying rather than recorded directly.
items.cn: satis 意为「足够」；其更深来源被重构为一个表示「满足」的词根，而非直接记录。

items.en: Satur 'full, sated' described a person or vessel that had taken all it wanted.
items.cn: satur「满的、饱足的」描述已取得所要之量的人或容器。

items.en: Saturare 'to fill' produced the participle saturatus, literally 'filled', which English borrowed as an adjective.
items.cn: saturare「填满」产生分词 saturatus，字面即「被填满的」，英语把它借作形容词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry applied the participle to solutions that could take no more solute and to fats whose chains were full of hydrogen.
items.cn: 十九世纪化学把这个分词用于再溶不进溶质的溶液，以及链上已充满氢的脂肪。

items.en: The same participle came to describe markets, colours and schedules that are full to their limit, with no room for more.
items.cn: 同一分词也用于满到极限、再无余地的市场、色彩与日程。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin root behind satis is a reconstruction, and its connection with words for sowing is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：satis 背后的拉丁语之前词根属于重构，它与表示播种的词之间的联系是假说，而非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds the verb and noun of the same family; group two holds adjectives for something completely filled or its opposite.
note.cn: 第一组是同一家族的动词与名词；第二组是表示完全填满或其反面的形容词。

entries.definition: The action of filling to capacity; saturated is the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 填到容量上限的动作；saturated 是产生的结果状态。

entries.definition: The state or process of being full; it can also mean colour intensity and market fullness.
entries.definitionCN: 填满的状态或过程；也可指色彩强度与市场饱和。

entries.definition: From satiare 'to satisfy an appetite': fully fed or bored, said of desires rather than of solutions or fats.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 satiare「满足食欲」：吃饱或腻了，用于欲望，而非溶液或脂肪。

entries.definition: Built on satis plus facere: content because a standard has been met, with no image of a full vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 由 satis 加 facere 构成：因达到标准而满意，不含装满容器的意象。

entries.definition: The plain word for something made thoroughly wet; saturated is its more technical and stronger counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示彻底湿透的日常词；saturated 是更技术、语气更强的对应词。

entries.definition: Wet through by rain or a wave; it stresses the cause, while saturated stresses the limit of absorption.
entries.definitionCN: 被雨或浪浇透；强调成因，而 saturated 强调吸收极限。

entries.definition: The broad adjective for a container with no space left; saturated adds that the material itself has absorbed the maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 表示容器没空间的通用形容词；saturated 进一步说明材料本身已吸收到极限。

entries.definition: Not filled to the limit; used of fats with double bonds and of solutions that can still dissolve more.
entries.definitionCN: 未填到极限；用于含双键的脂肪与仍能溶解更多的溶液。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Satur 'full': the ending -ated marks a state that has already been reached.
normal.cn: satur「满的」：词尾 -ated 标记已经达到的状态。

normal.en: The family runs saturate, saturated, saturation, unsaturated, supersaturated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 saturate、saturated、saturation、unsaturated、supersaturated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: saturated fat, saturated solution, saturated soil, saturated market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分义项：饱和脂肪、饱和溶液、浸透的土壤、饱和的市场。

normal.en: Chemistry counts bonds: saturated fats have only single bonds, unsaturated ones have double bonds.
normal.cn: 化学数键：饱和脂肪只有单键，不饱和脂肪含双键。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the participle ending -ed, so it always describes a completed filling.
normal.cn: 拼写保留分词词尾 -ed，因此它总描述已完成的填满。

abstract.en: Picture a cloth lifted from a bucket, water running from every corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布从桶里提起，水从每个角往下流。

abstract.en: Picture a jar packed with coins until the lid will not close.
abstract.cn: 想象一个罐子塞满硬币，盖子合不上。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with every square already written on.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，每一格都已写满。

examples.en: A saturated solution can be recognised by the crystals that remain at the bottom.
examples.cn: 饱和溶液可以通过杯底留下的晶体辨认出来。

examples.en: Doctors advise replacing saturated fat with unsaturated oils.
examples.cn: 医生建议用不饱和油替代饱和脂肪。

examples.en: The ground was saturated, so the water ran into the road instead of soaking away.
examples.cn: 地面已经浸透，水便流到路上而不是渗下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sat（足够）+ urated」——已经装到足够、再也装不下：饱和的、浸透的

root: 拉丁 saturatus「被填满的」，是 saturare（填满）的过去分词；saturare 出自 satur（满的），再上溯 satis（足够），其更早词根为重构。英语作形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one filled vessel: a solution stops dissolving, a fat chain fills with hydrogen, cloth and soil soak through, colour reaches full intensity, a market and a magnet reach their limits, an organic compound keeps only single bonds, and a schedule fills until nothing more fits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个被装满的容器：溶液停止溶解，脂肪链被氢填满，布与土壤浸透，颜色达到最饱满，市场与磁体到达极限，有机化合物只留单键，日程满到再也放不进东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth soaked until water runs from every corner when it is lifted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块布浸到提起时水从每个角往下流。

branches.en: CHEMICAL SATURATION: a solution at its ceiling and a chain full of hydrogen are the same 'no more can be added'.
branches.cn: 化学饱和：溶液到达上限与链被氢填满，都是「再也加不进」。

branches.en: FAT WITHOUT DOUBLE BONDS: the everyday nutrition sense comes straight from the bond count.
branches.cn: 无双键的脂肪：日常营养义直接来自键的计数。

branches.en: SOAKED MATERIAL: cloth and soil show the vessel image in its plainest form.
branches.cn: 浸透的材料：布与土壤以最朴素的形式展示容器意象。

branches.en: FULL INTENSITY AND FULL MARKETS: both colour and demand reach a point where nothing more is taken.
branches.cn: 饱满的强度与饱和的市场：颜色与需求都到达再也接纳不了更多的点。

branches.en: HARD LIMITS: a magnet and a full schedule both stop responding to further pressure.
branches.cn: 硬性极限：磁体与排满的日程都不再对更多压力作出反应。

intro.en: Saturated is a Latin participle used as an adjective, and its root of enough also builds words about satisfaction and fullness.
intro.cn: saturated 是一个作形容词用的拉丁分词，其「足够」词根也构成表示满足与充满的词。

latinIntro.en: Satur 'full' gives saturate, saturated and saturation; -ated marks a completed state, and un- reverses it in unsaturated.
latinIntro.cn: satur「满的」衍生 saturate、saturated 与 saturation；-ated 标记完成状态，un- 在 unsaturated 中将其反转。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「已经足够」的意思。

items.example: The adjective is the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族的核心。

items.example: The verb supplies the participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供分词。

items.example: The ending marks a state already reached.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记已经达到的状态。

items.example: The rain saturated the soil.
items.exampleCN: 雨水浸透了土壤。

items.example: The ground is saturated after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨后地面已浸透。

items.example: Saturation is reached at this temperature.
items.exampleCN: 在这个温度达到饱和。

items.example: The oil is unsaturated.
items.exampleCN: 这种油是不饱和的。

items.meaning: holding more than the normal limit
items.example: A supersaturated solution is unstable.
items.exampleCN: 过饱和溶液不稳定。

items.example: The diners were satiated.
items.exampleCN: 食客们已吃得饱足。

definition_zh: adj. 可耕的，适于耕种的（土地）　n. 耕地；种植业
definition_en: Of land, suitable for ploughing and growing crops rather than for pasture or trees; as a noun, arable land or crop farming.
core_image: 犁能翻得动、种得出粮的那片地
scene: 这一带只剩三成土地还能耕种。 Only thirty per cent of the land here is arable.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arable 修饰土地，指能犁能种庄稼，与牧场、林地相对。

pos.zh: 可耕的；适于耕种的
耕地；种植业

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（分类性形容词）

derivatives.zh: 可耕性
犁耕（旧词）
土地的；农业的
农业

senses.title: Land that can be ploughed
senses.definition: of soil or a field, in a condition that allows ploughing and the growing of crops
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤或田地的状况允许犁耕并种植作物
senses.example: The valley holds the only arable soil for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 方圆数英里只有这个山谷有可耕的土壤。
senses.why: The Latin root means plough and -able means able to be, so arable literally says able to be ploughed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「犁」，-able 意为「可被……的」，所以 arable 字面就是「犁得动的」。

senses.title: Crop farming as a category
senses.definition: in British farming use, arable land or arable as a noun, the branch of agriculture that grows crops rather than raising animals
senses.definitionCN: 英式农业用语中作名词，指种庄稼而非养牲畜的那一支农业
senses.example: The farm switched from dairy to arable in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场九十年代从奶牛转向了种植。
senses.why: Once the adjective named a kind of land, it could stand for that kind of farming, so the quality word became a category word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦指某类土地，就能进而指那类农业，于是表性质的词变成了表类别的词。

intro.en: Arable is Latin arabilis, that can be ploughed, from arare, to plough. The same ancient root gives Old English erian, to plough, and Greek arotos.
intro.cn: arable 就是拉丁语 arabilis「可犁的」，来自 arare「犁地」。同一古老词根还产生古英语 erian「犁」与希腊语 arotos。

items.en: The reconstructed root ar- meant to plough, one of the oldest farming words in the Indo-European family.
items.cn: 重构词根 ar- 意为「犁」，是印欧语系中最古老的农事词之一。

items.en: Latin arare meant to plough a field, the physical act of turning the soil with a blade.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arare 意为「犁田」，即用犁刀翻土这一实际动作。

items.en: Adding -abilis, able to be, gave arabilis, of land that will take the plough.
items.cn: 加上 -abilis「可被……的」得到 arabilis，指能吃得住犁的土地。

items.en: Old English erian, to plough, is the native cousin, which shows the root reached both branches.
items.cn: 古英语 erian「犁」是本族同源词，说明这个词根传到了两大支系。

items.en: French arable carried the Latin adjective into medieval Europe unchanged in shape and sense.
items.cn: 法语 arable 把这个拉丁形容词带入中世纪欧洲，形与义都没变。

items.en: English recorded arable in the fifteenth century, and British farming later made it a noun for crop growing.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪记录到 arable，后来英国农业把它用作指种植业的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against arid, which is the opposite kind of land, and parable, which only sounds similar; the near-meaning group gives other words for farmable ground.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与表示相反地况的 arid、以及只是音似的 parable 混淆；近义组给出其他表示可耕地的词。

entries.definition: A short story with a moral.

entries.definition: Living in or relating to trees.
entries.definitionCN: 树栖的；与树有关的。

entries.definition: Having the power to do.

normalIntro.en: Arable is ar-, plough, plus -able: land the plough can get through.
normalIntro.cn: arable 就是 ar-「犁」加 -able「能……的」：犁能翻得动的地。

normal.en: The fixed pair is arable land, opposed to pasture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 arable land，与 pasture 相对。

normal.en: Do not confuse arable with arid, which means dry.
normal.cn: 别把 arable 与 arid「干旱的」混淆。

normal.en: Arable farming grows crops; dairy farming keeps cows.
normal.cn: arable farming 种庄稼，dairy farming 养奶牛。

normal.en: There is no comparative: land is arable or it is not.
normal.cn: 没有比较级：地要么可耕，要么不可耕。

normal.en: In British use arable alone can be a noun.
normal.cn: 英式用法中 arable 可单独作名词。

abstract.en: Picture a blade turning dark soil in a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象犁刀把黑土翻成一条直线。

abstract.en: Imagine a map shaded only where crops can grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只在能种庄稼处上色的地图。

abstract.en: Think of stony ground that stops the plough dead.
abstract.cn: 想象让犁当场卡住的石质地。

examples.en: Erosion has cut the arable area by a fifth.
examples.cn: 侵蚀使可耕面积减少了五分之一。

examples.en: The village lost its arable land to the new road.
examples.cn: 村里的耕地被新建公路占去了。

examples.en: They grow wheat on every arable field they have.
examples.cn: 他们在每一块可耕的田里都种小麦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ar-「犁」+ -able「能……的」——犁得动、种得出粮，就是可耕的 arable。

root: 原始印欧词根 ar-「犁」生出拉丁 arare「犁地」，加 -abilis 成 arabilis「可犁的」，经法语进入英语作 arable；古英语 erian 与希腊 arotos 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses follow the plough: land the plough can enter, and the kind of farming that lives on such land.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都跟着犁走：犁能进得去的地，以及靠这种地吃饭的那类农业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the plot the plough can turn and crops can come out of
core.cn: 核心意象：犁能翻得动、种得出粮的那片地

branches.en: A valley of dark ploughable soil.
branches.cn: 一片黑土可犁的山谷。

branches.en: Stony ground the blade cannot enter.
branches.cn: 犁刀进不去的石质地。

branches.en: A farm switching from cows to wheat.
branches.cn: 从养牛转种小麦的农场。

branches.en: Arable as a branch of agriculture.
branches.cn: 作为农业一支的种植业。

branches.en: Both are defined by the plough.
branches.cn: 两者都由犁来定义。

intro.en: Arable is the plough root ar- plus -able; the field root agr- builds agriculture and agrarian beside it.
intro.cn: arable 是「犁」词根 ar- 加 -able；旁边的「田」词根 agr- 构成 agriculture 与 agrarian。

definition_en: to have a particular feature as the mark that identifies, defines or typifies the thing described
core_image: 一块木牌上刻着一道深痕，检验员不看整块木料，只凭这道痕就认出它属于哪一批
scene: 地质队员站在一处河谷前，向导指着两岸的红色岩壁，说认出这套地层靠的是颗粒粗细与胶结物的颜色。 The red beds can be characterized by coarse grains and iron cement.
sceneCN: 向导在河谷边讲解地层（第 1 个义项：以某事物为主要特征）；句意为这套红色地层以粗颗粒与铁质胶结物为特征。图中可辨识物件：红色岩壁、地质锤、放大镜、记录本。

senses.title: The main distinguishing feature
senses.definition: to have a particular feature as the most noticeable or identifying quality of the thing
senses.definitionCN: 以某个特征作为事物最显著或最具识别力的性质
senses.example: The old town can be characterized by narrow lanes and stone arches.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城以窄巷与石拱为主要特征。
senses.why: The Greek word behind the phrase meant an engraved mark, so a feature is treated as a mark cut into the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语背后的希腊词意为刻下的印记，因此特征被当作刻在事物上的一道痕。

senses.title: Defining a class or type
senses.definition: to have a feature that defines a category and separates it from neighbouring categories
senses.definitionCN: 具有某个特征，该特征定义一个类别并把它与相邻类别区分开
senses.example: The plant family can be characterized by four petals and a square stem.
senses.exampleCN: 这个植物科以四枚花瓣与方形茎为定义特征。
senses.why: In taxonomy a mark is used to sort specimens, so the phrase became a tool for definition rather than description.
senses.whyCN: 在分类学里标记用来分拣标本，于是这个短语成为定义的工具，而不只是描写。

senses.title: Showing signs or symptoms
senses.definition: to present a visible sign or symptom that indicates a condition
senses.definitionCN: 表现出某种可见迹象或症状，从而提示某种状况
senses.example: The early stage can be characterized by mild fever and fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 早期阶段表现为轻微发热与乏力。
senses.why: A symptom is a mark the body displays, and diagnosis reads marks the way an inspector reads a stamp.
senses.whyCN: 症状是身体显示出来的印记，诊断读这些印记，就像检验员读一枚戳记。

senses.title: A mark of a period or style
senses.titleCN: 以某事物为标志（时期风格）
senses.definition: to be marked by a style or practice that typifies a historical period
senses.definitionCN: 以某种典型化某个历史时期的风尚或做法为标志
senses.example: That period can be characterized by rapid urban growth and cheap printing.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时期以快速的城市扩张与廉价印刷为标志。
senses.why: Historians pick one trait as the stamp of an age, and the phrase turns a period into a marked object.
senses.whyCN: 历史学家挑出一个特征作为时代的戳记，这个短语就把一个时期变成带印记的对象。

senses.title: Dominated by a factor
senses.definition: to have one dominant factor that shapes the conditions of a region or zone
senses.definitionCN: 由某个主导因素塑造一个地区或地带的状况
senses.example: The region can be characterized by long dry summers and mild winters.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区以漫长干燥的夏季与温和的冬季为特征。
senses.why: A climate zone is named by its controlling factor, so the feature is not a detail but the ruling condition.
senses.whyCN: 气候带以控制性因素命名，因此这里的特征不是细节，而是主导条件。

senses.title: A typical method
senses.definition: to have a method or approach that is typical of a person, school or discipline
senses.definitionCN: 具有某种典型体现某个人、学派或学科的方法
senses.example: His fieldwork can be characterized by patient observation rather than quick sampling.
senses.exampleCN: 他的田野工作以耐心观察而非快速取样为典型。
senses.why: A method leaves the same kind of fingerprint as a style, so the phrase extends from objects to ways of working.
senses.whyCN: 方法留下的指纹与风格相同，于是这个短语从对象扩展到工作方式。

senses.title: A property of a material
senses.definition: to have a measurable property that distinguishes a material or substance
senses.definitionCN: 具有某种可测量的性质，从而区分一种材料或物质
senses.example: The alloy can be characterized by high strength at low weight.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金以低重量下的高强度为特性。
senses.why: Materials testing records numbers as marks, and a distinctive property becomes the signature of the substance.
senses.whyCN: 材料检测把数值记为标记，而独特性质就成为这种物质的签名。

senses.title: Depicted by a trait in literature
senses.definition: to be portrayed in a story through one defining trait or habit
senses.definitionCN: 在故事中通过某一项定义性特质或习惯被刻画出来
senses.example: In the novel, the hero can be characterized by stubborn loyalty.
senses.exampleCN: 在小说里，主人公以固执的忠诚为刻画特征。
senses.why: A fictional person is also a character, a marked figure, and one trait can serve as the engraving.
senses.whyCN: 虚构人物也是一个「角色」，一个带印记的形象，一项特质就足以充当那道刻痕。

intro.en: Characterize comes from Greek kharaktēr, an engraved mark or stamp, from kharassein, to scratch or engrave. The word reached English through Latin character, and the verb was formed with -ize.
intro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语「kharaktēr」「刻痕、印记」，更早出自「kharassein」「刻、雕」。它经拉丁语「character」进入英语，再加「-ize」构成动词。

items.en: Kharaktēr named a mark cut or stamped into a surface, a distinctive imprint rather than a general quality.
items.cn: 「kharaktēr」指刻在或压印在表面上的痕迹，是可辨认的印记，而非笼统的性质。

items.en: The verb kharassein meant to scratch, engrave or carve, and it supplied the action behind the mark.
items.cn: 动词「kharassein」意为抓刻、雕琢或雕刻，为这道印记提供了动作来源。

items.en: Latin took character for a mark, stamp or distinctive sign, and the sense of a written sign survived in English.
items.cn: 拉丁语用「character」表示记号、戳记或独特标志，书写符号的意思在英语里保留下来。

items.en: English character came to mean a distinguishing trait of a person, and later a person in a story.
items.cn: 英语「character」进而指一个人的独特特质，后来又指故事里的人物。

items.en: Characterize was formed on character with -ize, meaning to mark out or describe the distinctive quality of something.
items.cn: 「characterize」由「character」加「-ize」构成，意为标出或描述某事物的独特性质。

items.en: The passive phrase be characterized by became a standard frame in science, history and literary description.
items.cn: 被动短语「be characterized by」成为科学、历史与文学描写的标准框架。

note.en: The first group looks like character and shares its root; the second group contrasts three ways of linking things: characterized by names a defining mark, associated with reports a link that may be statistical or social, and composed of names the parts of a whole.
note.cn: 第一组与「character」形近且同源；第二组对照三种连接方式：「characterized by」指出定义性标志，「associated with」表示可能是统计或社交的联系，「composed of」指出构成整体的部分。

entries.definition: A distinguishing trait of a person, a written sign, or a figure in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人的独特特质、书写符号，或故事里的人物。

entries.definition: A feature that marks out a person or thing, or the adjective for such a feature.
entries.definitionCN: 指标出一个事物或人的特征，也指具有这种特征的。

entries.definition: To describe or identify the distinctive quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指描述或识别某事物的独特性质。

entries.definition: The act of describing a thing's features, or the portrayal of a figure in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 指描述事物特征的行为，或故事中对人物的刻画。

entries.definition: A comic exaggeration of a person; it looks close but comes from a different Italian word for loading.
entries.definitionCN: 指对人物的滑稽夸张；形近但来自另一个表示装载的意大利语词。

entries.definition: To show a visible sign of something; closer to a physical mark than to a defining rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示出某事物的可见迹象；更接近物理印记，而非定义规则。

entries.definition: To have something as the condition that fixes the identity of a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某事物作为确定事物身份的条件。

entries.definition: To be merely linked, often statistically or socially; a link may exist without being a defining mark.
entries.definitionCN: 指仅仅存在联系，常是统计或社交上的；这种联系未必构成定义性标志。

entries.definition: To consist of parts; it names the material or members, not the identifying feature.
entries.definitionCN: 指由部分组成；它说明材料或成员，而非识别特征。

entries.definition: To be represented by a typical example or feature of a whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 指以一个典型例子或特征来代表整个类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek mark behind the word and the settings where the phrase does its work.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后真实的希腊「刻痕」，以及该短语真正发挥作用的场景。

normal.en: The Greek word meant a groove cut into a surface, so a feature is a mark you can point to.
normal.cn: 希腊词意为刻在表面的一道槽，因此特征就是你能指出来的一道痕。

normal.en: Character, characteristic, characterize and characterization all keep the same engraved mark.
normal.cn: 「character」「characteristic」「characterize」「characterization」都保留着同一道刻痕。

normal.en: A stamp on a wooden tag tells an inspector which batch the timber belongs to.
normal.cn: 木牌上的戳记告诉检验员这批木料属于哪一批。

normal.en: In biology the phrase sorts specimens, while in statistics the neighbouring phrase only records a link.
normal.cn: 在生物学里这个短语用来分拣标本，而在统计学里相邻的那个短语只记录联系。

normal.en: A character in a novel can be characterized by one habit, the way a person is known by one scar.
normal.cn: 小说人物可以一个习惯为刻画特征，就像一个人靠一道疤被认出来。

abstract.en: A feature is evidence that someone could read the thing before meeting it.
abstract.cn: 特征是那件东西还没露面时，别人就已能读出它的证据。

abstract.en: To name the mark of a thing is to claim that the mark and the thing cannot be separated.
abstract.cn: 说出一个事物的标志，就是声称这个标志与事物无法分开。

abstract.en: Characterization is engraving done after the fact: the trait is chosen, then cut in.
abstract.cn: 刻画是事后的雕刻：先挑出特质，再把它刻进去。

examples.en: Desert plants can be characterized by thick leaves and deep roots.
examples.cn: 沙漠植物以厚叶与深根为特征。

examples.en: The second movement can be characterized by a slow, repeated rhythm.
examples.cn: 第二乐章以缓慢重复的节奏为特征。

examples.en: The patient's condition can be characterized by fever and a dry cough.
examples.cn: 病人的状况表现为发热与干咳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 克拉克特莱兹德 拜」——木板上刻一道痕，靠这道痕认整批木料：以……为特征

root: 希腊语「kharaktēr」「刻痕、印记」来自「kharassein」「刻、雕」；经拉丁语「character」进入英语，加「-ize」构成「characterize」，再加被动框架「be ... by」。它的核心是「可辨认的印记」，说的是识别标志，而不是组成部分，也不是统计关联。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a single visible feature to classification, symptoms, period style, climate, method, material property and literary portrayal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个可见特征，扩展到分类、症状、时期风格、气候、方法、材料属性与文学刻画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deep groove cut into a wooden tag lets an inspector name the whole batch at a glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：木牌上刻着一道深痕，检验员一眼就能叫出整批木料的名字。

branches.en: THE IDENTIFYING MARK: a feature that names the thing or sorts it into a class.
branches.cn: 识别标志：一个特征为事物命名，或把它归入某类。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE SIGN: symptoms and phenomena that show what is happening.
branches.cn: 可见迹象：症状与现象显示出正在发生什么。

branches.en: THE PERIOD AND CLIMATE MARK: a style of an age, or the dominant factor of a zone.
branches.cn: 时期与气候标志：一个时代的风尚，或一个地带的主导因素。

branches.en: THE TYPICAL METHOD AND MATERIAL: a way of working, or a property of a substance.
branches.cn: 典型方法与材料：一种工作方式，或一种材料的属性。

branches.en: THE LITERARY PORTRAIT: a character drawn by one defining trait.
branches.cn: 文学肖像：用一项定义性特质刻画的人物。

intro.en: The word is built on a Greek noun for an engraved mark, carried into Latin and then fitted with English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在一个表示「刻痕」的希腊名词上，经拉丁语传入后再装上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies kharaktēr and kharassein, Latin supplies character, and English adds -ize, -istic and -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「kharaktēr」与「kharassein」，拉丁语提供了「character」，英语再加上「-ize」「-istic」与「-ation」。

items.example: The mark was cut in so that it could be read later.
items.exampleCN: 这道痕迹被刻进去，以便日后辨认。

items.example: The verb names the cutting that makes the mark.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指造成痕迹的刻划动作。

items.example: Latin kept the sense of a stamped or written sign.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了压印或书写符号的意思。

items.meaning: personality; written symbol; figure in a story
items.example: The English noun widened from a sign to a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词从符号扩展到了人。

items.example: It names the feature that marks the thing.
items.exampleCN: 它指那个标出事物的特征。

items.meaning: to mark out or describe the nature of
items.example: The verb turns the mark into an act of description.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把印记变成描述的行为。

items.example: The noun names the finished portrait.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指完成的肖像。

items.meaning: to make or give a quality
items.example: The suffix turns a noun of quality into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把表示性质的名词变成动词。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾用同一词干构成形容词。

definition_zh: 自动化的；自动运行的；由机器自动完成的
definition_en: made to operate by machines or software with little or no human control
core_image: 深夜的车间里没有人，机械臂按程序依次抓取、焊接、放下，传送带不停地把成品送走
scene: 仓库的夜里只亮着几盏指示灯，分拣机器人按订单把包裹送进不同的滑道。 An automated warehouse keeps working long after the staff have gone home.
sceneCN: 这里指由机器按程序自行运转、几乎不需要人操作的（第 1 个义项：自动运行的）；句意：自动化仓库在员工回家后仍持续运转。

pos.zh: 自动化的；自动运行的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词回溯的动词形式，义为「使自动化」
由该动词加动作名词尾构成，义为「自动化」
由同一希腊词根构成，义为「自动的」
由「自动的」加副词词尾构成，义为「自动地」
由希腊语「自行动作者」借入，义为「自动装置」

senses.title: Running by itself
senses.definition: describing a machine or system that carries out its work without an operator
senses.definitionCN: 指无需操作员即可完成工作的机器或系统
senses.example: The automated line runs through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这条自动化生产线通宵运转。
senses.why: The word is the past participle of a verb meaning to make self-acting, so it describes something already set to run itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「使自行运作」这一动词的过去分词，因此描述已被设定为自行运转的事物。

senses.title: Governed by a control system
senses.definition: describing equipment whose actions are directed by sensors and controllers rather than hands
senses.definitionCN: 指动作由传感器与控制器而非人手指挥的设备
senses.example: An automated valve closes when the pressure rises.
senses.exampleCN: 压力升高时，自动阀门会关闭。
senses.why: A control loop replaces the human hand, so the word also marks the system that does the governing.
senses.whyCN: 控制回路替代了人手，因此这个词也标记执行支配的那个系统。

senses.title: Needing no human labour
senses.definition: describing a procedure completed without human effort or intervention
senses.definitionCN: 指无需人力或人工干预即可完成的流程
senses.example: The automated check takes a second per file.
senses.exampleCN: 自动检查每个文件只花一秒。
senses.why: If a task has no human step, its name shifts to the absence of labour, which is the practical meaning of automation.
senses.whyCN: 若一项任务没有人的步骤，其名称就转向「没有人力」，这正是自动化的实际含义。

senses.title: Factory work done by machines
senses.titleCN: 由机器完成的工厂作业
senses.definition: describing production in which machines handle materials and tools
senses.definitionCN: 指由机器处理材料与工具的生产方式
senses.example: The automated plant employs half the staff it once did.
senses.exampleCN: 这座自动化工厂的员工数只有过去的一半。
senses.why: Manufacturing was the first large field to adopt the word, so it became the standard label for machine-run production.
senses.whyCN: 制造业最早大规模采用这个词，因此它成了机器化生产的标准标签。

senses.title: Mechanical and unthinking
senses.definition: describing behaviour that is repeated without thought, as if performed by a machine
senses.definitionCN: 指不加思考地重复、仿佛由机器执行的行为
senses.example: His automated reply never changed a word.
senses.exampleCN: 他那机械的回复一个字都没变过。
senses.why: When human actions copy machine regularity, the same word describes the loss of thought.
senses.whyCN: 当人的行为复制机器的规律性，同一个词就描述思考的缺失。

senses.title: Generated without a person
senses.definition: describing a report, message or record produced by software rather than written by hand
senses.definitionCN: 指由软件而非手工撰写的报告、信息或记录
senses.example: The automated report arrives every Monday at six.
senses.exampleCN: 自动报告每周一六点送达。
senses.why: Output produced without an author is described by the same participle, extending the word from motion to text.
senses.whyCN: 没有作者产出的内容也用同一个分词描述，把这个词从运动扩展到文本。

senses.title: Self-driving vehicles
senses.definition: describing a vehicle that steers and brakes without a human driver
senses.definitionCN: 指无需人类驾驶即可转向与刹车的车辆
senses.example: The automated shuttle follows a fixed loop.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆自动驾驶摆渡车沿固定环线行驶。
senses.why: Driving is a continuous control task, so a machine that takes it over is described by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶是持续的控制任务，因此接管它的机器也用同一个词描述。

senses.title: Data handled by software
senses.definition: describing data work such as sorting, checking or formatting done by a program
senses.definitionCN: 指由程序完成的分拣、核对或格式化等数据工作
senses.example: Automated sorting cut the backlog in half.
senses.exampleCN: 自动分拣把积压减少了一半。
senses.why: Software can repeat a data step far faster than people, so the participle also labels machine-run data work.
senses.whyCN: 软件能比人快得多地重复数据步骤，因此这个分词也标记机器完成的数据工作。

intro.en: Automated descends from Greek autos, self, through automaton and automatic; the verb automate and its participle are modern.
intro.cn: 这个词经「自动装置」「自动的」上溯到希腊语「自己」；动词与分词形式则是现代产物。

items.en: Autos meant self, and its combining form auto- still begins many English words about self-action.
items.cn: 这个词意为「自己」，其组合形式至今出现在许多表示「自行」的英语词开头。

items.en: Automatos meant self-acting or self-moving, and it described things that move without an outside push.
items.cn: 这个词意为「自行动作、自行移动」，描述无需外力推动就会动的东西。

items.en: English borrowed automaton in the seventeenth century for a machine that seems to move itself, such as a clockwork figure.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入「自动装置」一词，指看似自行运动的机器，如发条人偶。

items.en: The adjective automatic extended the idea from clockwork toys to any mechanism that works by itself.
items.cn: 形容词「自动的」把这一观念从发条玩具扩展到任何自行工作的机械。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century industry formed the verb automate and the noun automation for replacing human operation with machines.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶，工业界造出动词「使自动化」与名词「自动化」，指用机器替代人工操作。

items.en: The first recorded use of the verb automate is generally placed in the mid-twentieth century, but the exact date and source are not established.
items.cn: 动词的首见一般定在二十世纪中叶，但确切年代与出处尚未确证。

note.en: The first group shares the self-acting stem; the second group describes machine-run work with other emphases.
note.cn: 第一组共享「自行动作」的词干；第二组以其他侧重描述机器完成的工作。

entries.definition: Working by itself; it is the older and broader adjective, while the target word often implies a process already converted.
entries.definitionCN: 自行工作的；是更早更宽的形容词，而目标词常暗示流程已被改造完成。

entries.definition: To convert a process to machine operation; the target word is its completed participle.
entries.definitionCN: 把流程改为机器操作；目标词是它的已完成分词。

entries.definition: The process or state of replacing human work with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器替代人工的过程或状态。

entries.definition: In a self-acting way; it modifies the action rather than describing the system.
entries.definitionCN: 以自行运作的方式；修饰动作，而不是描述系统。

entries.definition: Equipped with machinery; it stresses the machines themselves more than the removal of human control.
entries.definitionCN: 配备了机械的；更强调机器本身，而不是人控制的消失。

entries.definition: Operating without a crew; it is used mainly of vehicles and craft.
entries.definitionCN: 无乘员运行的；主要用于交通工具与飞行器。

entries.definition: Set in advance by instructions; it stresses the instructions rather than the absence of people.
entries.definitionCN: 由指令预先设定的；强调指令，而不是人的缺席。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root and the real automation family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的自动化词族。

normal.en: Autos means self, so automated means made to act by itself.
normal.cn: 「自己」加动作，自动化的就是被设定为自行运作的。

normal.en: The family runs automate, automated, automation, automatic and automatically.
normal.cn: 同族词有使自动化、自动化的、自动化、自动的与自动地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the system: automated system, automated process, fully automated.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出系统：自动化系统、自动化流程、全自动的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the application: automated warehouse, automated driving, automated response.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用：自动化仓库、自动驾驶、自动回复。

normal.en: The clockwork figure is the ancestor image: a body that moves without being pushed.
normal.cn: 发条人偶是祖先画面：没有被推却会动的人形。

abstract.en: Picture a factory where the lights stay on but no footsteps are heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂，灯一直亮着，却听不到脚步声。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that writes the same letter a thousand times without ever looking up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手写同一个字母一千遍，从不抬头。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that winds itself whenever the weight falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，重锤下落时它就给自己上弦。

examples.en: The automated gate opens only for registered cars.
examples.cn: 自动闸门只对登记过的车辆开放。

examples.en: Fully automated factories still need engineers for repairs.
examples.cn: 全自动工厂仍需工程师维修。

examples.en: The automated email went to thousands of customers by mistake.
examples.cn: 那封自动邮件被误发给了数千名客户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥托」自己会动——奥托是个不用人推的机器 → 自动化的

root: 希腊语「自己」加表示「自行动作」的希腊语形式；经「自动装置」「自动的」进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow self-action from machines to control systems, labour, factories, human habit, generated text, driving and data work.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「自行动作」展开：机器、控制系统、人力、工厂、人的习惯、生成的文本、驾驶与数据工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mechanism that begins to work without a hand on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台没有手去触碰却开始工作的机械。

branches.en: THE MACHINE ITSELF: a line or a plant that runs without an operator.
branches.cn: 机器本身：无需操作员即可运转的生产线或工厂。

branches.en: THE GOVERNOR: sensors and controllers that steer the equipment.
branches.cn: 支配者：操纵设备的传感器与控制器。

branches.en: THE WORK WITHOUT HANDS: procedures and data steps completed by software.
branches.cn: 无需人手的工作：由软件完成的流程与数据步骤。

branches.en: THE HUMAN IMITATION: behaviour repeated without thought, like a machine.
branches.cn: 人的模仿：不加思考地重复、形同机器的行为。

branches.en: SELF-PRODUCED OUTPUT AND SELF-DRIVEN MOVEMENT: generated reports, and vehicles that steer themselves.
branches.cn: 自生成的产出与自驱动的移动：自动生成的报告，以及自行转向的车辆。

intro.en: Automated is a Greek-rooted word wearing English endings; its stem reaches English through three separate borrowings.
intro.cn: 这个词以希腊语为词根，披着英语词尾；其词干通过三次独立借入进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, not Latin; Latin contributed only the shape of the adjective ending, so no Latin cognate of the root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语；拉丁语只提供了形容词词尾的形式，因此不列出该词根的拉丁同族词。

items.structure: Greek pronoun used as a combining form
items.example: The root supplies the self in self-acting.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「自行」中的那个「自」。

items.meaningCN: 自行动作的；自行移动的
items.example: The adjective describes what moves without an outside push.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述无需外力推动就会动的东西。

items.example: The clockwork figure was the first English automaton.
items.exampleCN: 发条人偶是英语中最早的自动装置。

items.example: The adjective widened the idea beyond toys.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把观念扩展到玩具之外。

items.example: Factories automate the steps people used to repeat.
items.exampleCN: 工厂把人过去重复的步骤自动化。

items.example: The ending marks a process already converted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记流程已被改造完成。

items.example: Automation names the whole change, not one machine.
items.exampleCN: 「自动化」指整个转变，而不是某一台机器。

items.example: The system restarts automatically after a fault.
items.exampleCN: 系统在故障后自动重启。

definition_zh: 编辑；校订；剪辑；删改；主编；编辑版本
definition_en: to revise and improve a text, prepare it for publication, cut or rearrange material, or change digital content
core_image: 一双手在稿纸上删、改、挪：把多余的部分剪掉，让留下的部分更清楚。
scene: 编辑花了一上午，把一段长长的文字删改成三个清楚的句子。 The editor spent the morning editing a long paragraph down to three clear sentences.
sceneCN: 这里 edit 是「删改文字、让表达更清楚」（第 1 个义项：修订文稿）；句意：编辑花了一上午，把一段长文字改成了三个清楚的句子。场景要点：红笔、划掉的行、页边批注。

pos.zh: 编辑；校订；剪辑；删改；主编
编辑版本；一次编辑改动

derivatives.zh: 编辑；主编；剪辑者

senses.title: Revise a text
senses.titleCN: 校订文字：删、改、调整，让它更准确清楚
senses.definition: to read a piece of writing and change it in order to improve accuracy, clarity, or style
senses.definitionCN: 阅读一篇文字并作出修改，使其更准确、清楚或更合风格
senses.example: She edited the report twice before sending it to the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她把报告改了两遍才发给董事会。
senses.why: Latin edere meant 'to give out, bring forth'. Editing is the work that makes a text fit to be brought out in public: what cannot stand is removed, what is unclear is fixed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 edere 意为“拿出来、产出”。编辑就是让文本适合公开“拿出来”的工作：站不住的内容删掉，不清楚的地方改好。

senses.title: Prepare for publication as editor
senses.titleCN: 主编：对整份出版物的内容负责
senses.definition: to be in charge of preparing a newspaper, magazine, or book for publication
senses.definitionCN: 负责把报纸、杂志或书准备到可出版的状态
senses.example: For ten years she edited the country's leading science magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 她主编这个国家最重要的科学杂志长达十年。
senses.why: The person who edits in this sense does not just fix sentences; they decide what enters the publication and what is left out. Editing becomes a form of gatekeeping.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项里的编辑不只改句子，还决定什么能进出版物、什么被挡在外面。编辑由此变成一种守门。

senses.title: Remove by editing
senses.titleCN: 删掉：把不该出现的部分剪出去
senses.definition: to remove words, scenes, or data from a text or recording
senses.definitionCN: 从文字或录音录像中移除词句、场景或数据
senses.example: The lawyer asked them to edit out the names of the children.
senses.exampleCN: 律师要求他们把孩子们的名字删掉。
senses.why: If editing is making a text fit to be shown, some material must be cut away. The phrasal verb edit out makes the cutting explicit: the piece is removed, not rewritten.
senses.whyCN: 如果编辑是让文本适合展示，就必须剪掉一些材料。短语动词 edit out 把这刀明说出来：那一块是被移走，而不是被改写。

senses.title: Cut and arrange film or sound
senses.titleCN: 剪辑：把拍好的片段重新排列成故事
senses.definition: to select and arrange shots or recorded sound to form a finished film or track
senses.definitionCN: 挑选并排列镜头或录音，形成完成的影片或音轨
senses.example: The director edited the scene so that the argument happens in silence.
senses.exampleCN: 导演重新剪了这个场景，让争吵发生在静默中。
senses.why: Film editing is the same operation as text editing, done with time instead of lines: keep this, drop that, move this earlier. The editor builds meaning by sequence.
senses.whyCN: 电影剪辑与文字编辑是同一个操作，只是用时间而不是行来做事：留这个、扔那个、把这个提前。剪辑者用顺序制造意义。

senses.title: Alter genetic material
senses.titleCN: 基因编辑：在生命的文本上改字
senses.definition: to change the DNA of an organism deliberately, adding, removing, or rewriting a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 有意改变生物的 DNA，增加、删除或改写一段序列
senses.example: The technique can edit a single letter in the genome.
senses.exampleCN: 这项技术能编辑基因组里的一个字母。
senses.why: DNA is written as a sequence of letters, so the language of editing transferred naturally. Gene editing treats the genome as a text that can be corrected at a specific position.
senses.whyCN: DNA 被写成字母序列，所以“编辑”的语言自然迁移过来。基因编辑把基因组当成一份可以在特定位置修正的文本。

senses.title: Adjust an image or photo
senses.titleCN: 修图：裁切、调色、去掉不要的部分
senses.definition: to change a photograph or image by cropping, adjusting colour, or removing elements
senses.definitionCN: 通过裁切、调色或移除元素来改变照片或图像
senses.example: He edited the photo to remove a stranger from the background.
senses.exampleCN: 他修了照片，把背景里的陌生人去掉。
senses.why: A photograph is now a file rather than a print, so changes are made by selection and deletion. The old editorial gestures — crop, cut, correct — survive in digital form.
senses.whyCN: 照片现在是文件而不是相纸，所以改动靠选取和删除完成。古老的编辑动作——裁、剪、改——以数字形式活了下来。

senses.title: Change data or a record
senses.titleCN: 修改数据：改动一条记录或一个字段
senses.definition: to change the contents of a file, database record, or settings field
senses.definitionCN: 改变文件、数据库记录或设置字段的内容
senses.example: Only administrators can edit the payment records.
senses.exampleCN: 只有管理员能修改付款记录。
senses.why: Any stored text can be edited: a record is a small document. In computing the word is neutral and technical, covering every deliberate change to stored content.
senses.whyCN: 任何被存下来的文本都能被编辑：一条记录就是一份小文档。在计算机里这个词中性而技术化，涵盖对存储内容的一切有意改动。

senses.title: Compile a collection
senses.titleCN: 编选文集：把多篇文字收成一本
senses.definition: to collect and prepare a group of texts, essays, or images for a single volume
senses.definitionCN: 收集并整理一组文字、文章或图像，编成一册
senses.example: Two historians edited a volume of letters from the war.
senses.exampleCN: 两位历史学家编了一卷战时书信集。
senses.why: An editor of a volume does not write it; they choose what belongs together and put it in order. Editing here is selecting and arranging, not rewriting.
senses.whyCN: 一卷文集的编者并不写它；他们选择哪些东西该放在一起，并把它们排好。这里的编辑是挑选与排列，而不是重写。

senses.title: One edited version or change
senses.titleCN: 编辑版本：一次改动后的成品
senses.definition: a version of a text or film after editing, or a single change made in an editing session
senses.definitionCN: 文字或影片编辑后的一个版本，或一次编辑中的单处改动
senses.example: The director's final edit is two minutes shorter than the cinema release.
senses.exampleCN: 导演的最终剪辑版比院线版短两分钟。
senses.why: The noun is the count version of the verb: an edit is one complete pass through the material, or one change produced by such a pass.
senses.whyCN: 名词是动词的可数版本：一次 edit 就是从头到尾处理一遍材料，或这一遍产生的某一处改动。

intro.en: Edit is a back-formation from editor, which English borrowed from Latin. The Latin verb edere meant 'to give out, bring forth' — publishing as bringing a work out into the open.
intro.cn: edit 是由 editor 逆构而成的，而 editor 是英语从拉丁语借来的。拉丁动词 edere 意为“拿出来、产出”——出版就是把作品带到公开之处。

items.en: Dare meant 'to give'. It is one of the most productive verbs in Latin, and it supplies the second half of edere.
items.cn: dare 意为“给”。它是拉丁语最能产的动词之一，也是 edere 的后半。

items.en: Edere meant 'to give out, bring forth, publish'. Its past participle editus is the source of edition, editor, and edit.
items.cn: edere 意为“给出、产出、出版”。它的过去分词 editus 是 edition、editor 与 edit 的来源。

items.en: Editor in Latin meant 'one who puts forth or publishes'. English borrowed it in the 17th century for the person who prepares a text.
items.cn: 拉丁语 editor 意为“拿出或出版某物的人”。英语在 17 世纪借入，指准备文本的人。

items.en: The verb edit is recorded in English in the late 18th century, most likely formed by removing the -or from editor. The noun came later.
items.cn: 动词 edit 于 18 世纪后期见于英语，很可能是从 editor 去掉 -or 逆构而来。名词义更晚。

items.en: As film, radio, and recording developed, edit extended from paper to shots and sound. The editor became the person who decides sequence.
items.cn: 随着电影、广播与录音的发展，edit 从纸张扩展到镜头与声音。编辑者成了决定顺序的人。

items.en: Word processors, photo software, databases, and gene technology all reuse the word. Anything represented as a sequence can now be edited.
items.cn: 文字处理软件、修图软件、数据库与基因技术都再次使用这个词。任何被表示为序列的东西，如今都能被编辑。

note.en: The first group is the edere/editor family; the second collects revise words, each with a different kind of change.
note.cn: 第一组是 edere/editor 词族；第二组收“修改”类近义词，每种改动方式不同。

entries.definition: a person who prepares texts or media for publication. English had editor before it had the verb edit.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字或媒体准备到可出版状态的人。英语先有 editor，后有动词 edit。

entries.definition: one published form of a book or newspaper. It comes from Latin editio 'a bringing forth'.
entries.definitionCN: 书或报纸的一个出版形态。它来自拉丁语 editio“产出”。

entries.definition: relating to editing or an editor; also a newspaper article stating the paper's opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 与编辑或主编有关的；也指表达报社立场的社论。

entries.definition: able to be edited. It applies the -able suffix to the verb edit.
entries.definitionCN: 可编辑的。它是把 -able 加到动词 edit 上。

entries.definition: to read again and change in order to improve. It stresses a second look; edit can also mean selecting and arranging.
entries.definitionCN: 重读并修改以求改进。它强调再看一遍；edit 还可指挑选与编排。

entries.definition: to make a small change, especially to a law or document. It is narrower and more official than edit.
entries.definitionCN: 对法律或文件作小改动。它比 edit 更窄、更正式。

entries.definition: to edit text for publication, especially to remove sensitive material. It comes from a different Latin root, redigere.
entries.definitionCN: 为出版而编辑文字，尤指删去敏感内容。它来自另一个拉丁词根 redigere。

entries.definition: to change something partly. It is broader than edit and does not imply improving or preparing for publication.
entries.definitionCN: 部分地改变某物。它比 edit 宽，不含“改进”或“准备出版”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin edere 'give out' (e- + dare), and the family editor, edition, editorial, editable, unedited.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 edere“拿出”（e- + dare），以及 editor、edition、editorial、editable、unedited 词族。

normal.en: Edit was cut out of editor, just as the editor cuts things out of a text.
normal.cn: edit 是从 editor 里剪出来的，就像编辑从文本里剪东西一样。

normal.en: The Latin base is e- 'out' + dare 'give': to edit is to make a text fit to be given out.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基是 e-“出”+ dare“给”：编辑就是让文本适合被“发出去”。

normal.en: Editor, edition, editorial all come from the same 'bring forth' verb.
normal.cn: editor、edition、editorial 都来自同一个“产出”动词。

normal.en: In film, editing is choosing which shots to keep and in what order — text editing with time.
normal.cn: 在电影里，剪辑是选择留哪些镜头、按什么顺序——用时间来做的文字编辑。

normal.en: Gene editing works because DNA is written as letters; the word 'edit' fits the material.
normal.cn: 基因编辑能成立，是因为 DNA 被写成字母；edit 这个词正好贴合这种材料。

abstract.en: Editing is the art of deciding what the reader will never know was there.
abstract.cn: 编辑的艺术，是决定读者永远不会知道那里曾有什么。

abstract.en: Every cut is an argument about what matters.
abstract.cn: 每一刀删改，都是一次关于“什么才重要”的论证。

abstract.en: A text becomes itself only after something has been taken away.
abstract.cn: 一个文本只有在被拿走一些东西之后，才真正成为它自己。

examples.en: The journal rejected the paper but asked the authors to edit it and resubmit.
examples.cn: 期刊拒了这篇论文，但请作者修改后再投。

examples.en: He edited the interview down to four minutes for the evening news.
examples.cn: 他把握了采访剪到四分钟，用于晚间新闻。

examples.en: Scientists used the tool to edit a gene linked to the disease.
examples.cn: 科学家用这个工具编辑了一个与疾病相关的基因。

dict_mnemonic.text: “挨得特”——挨得特拿红笔一行行挨着改，删到只剩重点 → edit 编辑、删改

root: 源自拉丁语 edere“拿出、产出、出版”，由 e-“向外”+ dare“给”构成；英语先有 editor，后逆构出动词 edit，核心是“把材料修整到适合拿出去”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of edit, all one operation: look at a body of material, then cut, change, and rearrange it until it is fit to be shown.
sensesIntro.cn: edit 的九个义项都是同一个操作：审视一堆材料，然后删、改、重排，直到它适合被展示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand with a red pen, crossing out, correcting, and moving lines on a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拿红笔，在纸页上划掉、改正、挪动句子。

branches.en: TEXT: revising sentences, running a publication, and compiling a volume are three levels of the same editorial care.
branches.cn: 文本：改句子、管出版物、编文集，是同一份编辑功夫的三个层级。

branches.en: REMOVAL: edit out a name, cut a scene — meaning is built as much by what is taken away.
branches.cn: 移除：删掉一个名字、剪掉一个场景——意义同样由被拿走的东西构成。

branches.en: MATERIAL AS TEXT: genes and pixels are handled as sequences that can be cut and rearranged like words.
branches.cn: 材料当文本：基因与像素被当作可像文字一样剪接、重排的序列。

branches.en: RECORDS: a database row is edited like a sentence — a field is changed and the old value is replaced.
branches.cn: 记录：数据库的一行也像句子一样被编辑——改一个字段，旧值被替换。

branches.en: PRODUCT: an edit is one finished pass, the countable result of all that cutting.
branches.cn: 成品：一次 edit 就是完整的一遍，是所有删改的可数结果。

intro.en: Edit's family comes from Latin edere through editor and edition. The suffixes mark the person, the version, the attitude, and the possibility of being changed.
intro.cn: edit 的词族经 editor 与 edition 来自拉丁语 edere。后缀分别标记人、版本、态度与“可被修改”的可能性。

latinIntro.en: The reliable Latin forms are edere 'to give out', its participle editus, and editor 'one who puts forth'. These explain both the 'publish' core and the back-formed English verb.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的拉丁形式是 edere“拿出”、其分词 editus，以及 editor“拿出某物的人”。它们解释了“出版”的核心与英语逆构动词的来历。

items.meaning: one who prepares text or media for publication
items.meaningCN: 把文字或媒体准备到可出版状态的人（-or 构成施事名词）
items.example: The editor returned the draft with thirty comments.
items.exampleCN: 编辑退回草稿，附了三十条意见。

items.meaning: one published version of a work
items.meaningCN: 一部作品的一个出版版本（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The second edition corrects several maps.
items.exampleCN: 第二版更正了几幅地图。

items.meaning: relating to editing or to an editor's opinion
items.meaningCN: 与编辑有关的；表达编者意见的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The paper published an editorial supporting the reform.
items.exampleCN: 报纸发表了一篇支持改革的社论。

items.meaning: in editorial matters, or as an editorial opinion
items.meaningCN: 在编辑事务上；作为编者意见（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The magazine is editorially independent of its owner.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志在编辑上独立于其所有者。

items.meaning: able to be changed or revised
items.meaningCN: 可编辑的；可修改的（-able 构成能力形容词）
items.example: The shared file is editable by everyone in the team.
items.exampleCN: 团队里每个人都能编辑这个共享文件。

items.meaningCN: 未经编辑或剪辑的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: The archive released the unedited interview for the first time.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆首次公布了未剪辑的采访。

items.meaning: to edit again, often into a new version
items.meaningCN: 重新编辑；再剪一版（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The studio re-edited the film for its tenth anniversary.
items.exampleCN: 制片厂为十周年重新剪辑了这部电影。

items.meaning: to correct grammar, style, and consistency in a text
items.meaningCN: 对文稿做文字校对与统一（copy + edit 复合）
items.example: A freelancer copy-edited the manuscript before typesetting.
items.exampleCN: 排版前由一位自由职业者做了文字校对。

items.meaning: to prepare copy under a senior editor
items.meaningCN: 在主编之下做文稿编辑（sub- 表示“在下”）
items.example: She sub-edited the business pages for two years.
items.exampleCN: 她在商业版做了两年副编辑。

items.meaning: to remove a part while editing
items.meaningCN: 编辑时删去某部分（out 表示“出去”）
items.example: They edited out the pause before his answer.
items.exampleCN: 他们剪掉了他回答前的停顿。

latinEntries.meaning: to give out, bring forth, publish
one who puts forth or publishes

definition_zh: 放射性碳；碳十四；放射性碳含量
definition_en: a radioactive form of carbon, especially carbon-14, used to date organic remains
core_image: 高空云层里，宇宙射线撞上氮原子，生成一小撮会缓慢衰变的碳，随雨水落进草木与骨骼
scene: 高空云层中，宇宙射线撞上氮原子，生成会缓慢衰变的碳原子，随雨水落进草木。 Cosmic rays strike nitrogen high in the atmosphere and produce radiocarbon that rains down into plants.
sceneCN: 这里 radiocarbon 指「具有放射性的碳同位素，主要是碳十四」（第 1 个义项：放射性碳）；句意为宇宙射线在高空撞击氮原子，生成随雨水落进植物的放射性碳。可辨识物件：高空云层、射线轨迹、草木、雨滴。

pos.zh: 放射性碳；碳十四；（口语）放射性碳测年

forms.label: 相关形容词（放射性测量的）
相关名词（放射性碳年龄）

derivatives.zh: radiocarbon（放射性碳）+ dating（测年）→ 放射性碳定年法
radiocarbon + age（年龄）→ 放射性碳年龄
radiocarbon + reservoir（储库）→ 放射性碳储库
radio-（放射）+ -metric（希腊 metron，测量）→ 放射性测量的
radio-（放射）+ -genic（希腊 -genēs，产生）→ 放射成因的
radiocarbon + calibrated（已校准的）→ 经放射性碳校准的
radiocarbon（放射性碳）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ 放射性碳的（罕用）

senses.title: Radioactive carbon
senses.definition: carbon that is radioactive, especially the isotope carbon-14
senses.definitionCN: 具有放射性的碳，尤指碳十四同位素
senses.example: Radiocarbon in the sample had decayed to half its original amount.
senses.exampleCN: 样品中的放射性碳已衰变到原来的一半。
senses.why: The word joins the radiation prefix to the element name, so it names a kind of carbon rather than a method.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把放射前缀与元素名连起来，命名的是碳的一种，而非方法。

senses.title: Carbon-14 by name
senses.definition: the isotope with six protons and eight neutrons, written carbon-14
senses.definitionCN: 含六个质子、八个中子的同位素，写作碳十四
senses.example: Radiocarbon is produced when cosmic rays hit nitrogen-14.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙射线撞击氮十四时产生放射性碳。
senses.why: In practice the word almost always means this one isotope, because it is the one useful for dating.
senses.whyCN: 在实际使用中，这个词几乎总指这一种同位素，因为它正是可用于测年的那一种。

senses.title: Carbon made in the atmosphere
senses.titleCN: 大气中生成的放射性碳
senses.definition: radiocarbon formed high in the air and mixed into the carbon cycle
senses.definitionCN: 在高空生成、进入碳循环的放射性碳
senses.example: Atmospheric radiocarbon doubled during the nuclear tests of the nineteen-fifties.
senses.exampleCN: 20 世纪 50 年代的核试验使大气放射性碳翻倍。
senses.why: The atmospheric source matters because it sets the baseline against which samples are compared.
senses.whyCN: 大气来源之所以重要，是因为它构成比较样品时的基线。

senses.title: Carbon inside living things
senses.definition: radiocarbon taken up by plants and passed along food chains
senses.definitionCN: 被植物吸收、再沿食物链传递的放射性碳
senses.example: Living tissue carries radiocarbon in proportion to the air it grew in.
senses.exampleCN: 活体组织携带的放射性碳与其生长时空气的比例相当。
senses.why: Because living things stop taking in new carbon at death, their radiocarbon becomes a clock.
senses.whyCN: 由于生物死后不再摄入新的碳，其体内的放射性碳就成了时钟。

senses.title: The carbon measured in a sample
senses.titleCN: 样品中用于测量的放射性碳
senses.definition: the residual radiocarbon in charcoal, bone or shell used for dating
senses.definitionCN: 木炭、骨骼或贝壳中残留、用于测年的放射性碳
senses.example: The laboratory extracted radiocarbon from a gram of charred wood.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室从一克炭化木材中提取了放射性碳。
senses.why: The word shifts from the substance in general to the portion that survives in a particular sample.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从泛指的物质，转到某一具体样品中残留的那一部分。

senses.title: The decay of radiocarbon
senses.definition: the process by which carbon-14 turns into nitrogen-14 with a half-life of about five thousand seven hundred years
senses.definitionCN: 碳十四以约五千七百年半衰期转变为氮十四的过程
senses.example: The slow decay of radiocarbon limits how far back the method can reach.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性碳的缓慢衰变限制了这种方法能回溯多远。
senses.why: The decay rate is the physical fact that turns the isotope into a measurable clock.
senses.whyCN: 衰变速率正是把这个同位素变成可测量时钟的物理事实。

senses.title: Radiocarbon concentration
senses.definition: the amount or activity of radiocarbon in a material, usually compared with a standard
senses.definitionCN: 材料中放射性碳的数量或活度，通常与标准比较
senses.example: The radiocarbon concentration of the shell was too low to measure precisely.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚贝壳的放射性碳含量太低，无法精确测量。
senses.why: Measurement works on concentration, so the word often names a quantity rather than a substance.
senses.whyCN: 测量依据的是浓度，因此这个词常指一个量而非一种物质。

senses.title: Radiocarbon dating, by shorthand
senses.titleCN: 放射性碳测年（口语简称）
senses.definition: the method of radiocarbon dating, named by its isotope in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中以同位素之名指放射性碳测年法
senses.example: The report says the bone was dated by radiocarbon.
senses.exampleCN: 报告说这块骨头是用放射性碳测年的。
senses.why: Metonymy lets the substance stand for the method, though careful writing keeps the two apart.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让物质代指方法，不过严谨的写作会把两者分开。

intro.en: Radiocarbon joins a Latin ray word to a Latin charcoal word, and its dating use comes from mid-twentieth-century physics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: radiocarbon 把拉丁语「射线」词与「炭」词连在一起，其测年用途来自 20 世纪中叶的物理学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin radius meant 'ray, beam, spoke'; the prefix radio- was later used for radiation and for radio.
items.cn: 拉丁 radius 意为「射线、梁、辐条」；前缀 radio- 后来用于放射与无线电。

items.en: Latin carbo, carbonis meant 'charcoal, ember', and English carbon was named from it after the element was identified.
items.cn: 拉丁 carbo（属格 carbonis）意为「木炭、炭火」，元素被确认后英语 carbon 即由此命名。

items.en: Carbon-14 is a rare radioactive isotope of carbon, produced in the upper air by cosmic rays striking nitrogen.
items.cn: 碳十四是碳的一种稀少放射性同位素，由宇宙射线在高空撞击氮生成。

items.en: Radiocarbon was coined in the twentieth century to name radioactive carbon, with radio- meaning radioactive rather than 'ray'.
items.cn: radiocarbon 是 20 世纪为指放射性碳而造的词，其中 radio- 意为「放射」而非字面的「射线」。

items.en: Willard Libby's method of the late nineteen-forties made radiocarbon the best-known natural clock in archaeology.
items.cn: 威拉德·利比在 40 年代后期的方法，使放射性碳成为考古学中最著名的天然时钟。

items.en: Source uncertain (first use): the compound has no single recorded coiner, and the half-life value has been refined several times, so older figures differ from the current convention.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见使用）：这个复合词没有单一可考的首创者；半衰期数值也经过多次修正，较早的数字与现行惯例不同。

note.en: Group one holds words built with radio- or carbon but meaning something else; group two holds the technical names of the same isotope and its relatives.
note.cn: 第一组是同用 radio- 或 carbon、却另有所指的词；第二组是同一同位素及其亲属的技术名称。

entries.definition: From Latin radius 'ray'; radium is a metal, not a form of carbon.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 radius「射线」；镭是金属，不是碳的一种形态。

entries.definition: Radius plus Greek graphein 'to write'; it names an image made by rays.
entries.definitionCN: radius 加希腊 graphein「写」；指用射线形成的影像。

entries.definition: Radio- plus metron 'measure'; it describes measurement of radiation, not carbon itself.
entries.definitionCN: radio- 加 metron「测量」；形容对放射性的测量，而非碳本身。

entries.definition: The element itself, from Latin carbo 'charcoal'; radiocarbon is one radioactive isotope of it.
entries.definitionCN: 元素本身，来自拉丁 carbo「木炭」；radiocarbon 是其一种放射性同位素。

entries.definition: The precise isotope name, preferred when the science must be unambiguous.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的同位素名称，科学表述需明确时首选。

entries.definition: Any form of an element with a particular neutron number; radiocarbon is one.
entries.definitionCN: 元素中具特定中子数的任一形式；放射性碳是其中一种。

entries.definition: Any radioactive nuclide, of which carbon-14 is a single example.
entries.definitionCN: 任何放射性核素，碳十四只是其中一例。

entries.definition: A nuclide produced by cosmic rays, the route by which natural radiocarbon forms.
entries.definitionCN: 由宇宙射线产生的核素，正是天然放射性碳的形成途径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin elements, the cosmic-ray production and the real laboratory vocabulary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、宇宙射线生成过程，以及真实的实验室词汇。

normal.en: Latin radius 'ray' gives the radio- prefix; Latin carbo 'charcoal' gives carbon.
normal.cn: 拉丁 radius「射线」给出 radio- 前缀；拉丁 carbo「木炭」给出 carbon。

normal.en: Cosmic rays hit nitrogen-14, and the result is carbon-14.
normal.cn: 宇宙射线撞击氮十四，产物是碳十四。

normal.en: The half-life is about five thousand seven hundred years.
normal.cn: 半衰期约为五千七百年。

normal.en: Real compounds: radiocarbon age, radiocarbon calibration, radiocarbon reservoir.
normal.cn: 真实复合词：放射性碳年龄、放射性碳校准、放射性碳储库。

normal.en: Careful writing separates the isotope from the dating method named after it.
normal.cn: 严谨写作会把同位素与以它命名的测年方法分开。

abstract.en: Picture a spark in the sky turning air into a slow clock.
abstract.cn: 想象天空中一道火花把空气变成一只慢时钟。

abstract.en: Picture rain carrying that clock into leaves and bones.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水把这只时钟带进叶子与骨骼。

abstract.en: Picture a grey number falling by half, again and again, over thousands of years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个灰色数字一次次减半，持续数千年。

examples.en: Radiocarbon from the atmosphere enters plants through photosynthesis.
examples.cn: 大气中的放射性碳通过光合作用进入植物。

examples.en: The laboratory measured radiocarbon in the collagen of the bone.
examples.cn: 实验室测量了骨骼胶原中的放射性碳。

examples.en: The review compared radiocarbon with other natural clocks.
examples.cn: 这篇综述把放射性碳与其他天然时钟做了比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「radio（放射）＋carbon（碳）」——会放射的碳 → 放射性碳

root: radio- 出拉丁 radius「射线」，20 世纪转指放射；carbon 出拉丁 carbo「木炭、炭火」。radiocarbon 为 20 世纪新造词，指放射性碳，主要为碳十四。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from radioactive carbon and its isotope name through atmospheric and living carbon, the portion in a sample, decay, concentration, and the everyday shorthand for the dating method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从放射性碳与其同位素名出发，经过大气与生物体内的碳、样品中的残留部分、衰变、含量，最后是日常口语中以它代指测年法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark in the sky making a slow clock that rains into living things.
core.cn: 核心意象：天空中一道火花造出一只慢时钟，随雨落进生物体内。

branches.en: THE ISOTOPE: the word names radioactive carbon, above all carbon-14.
branches.cn: 同位素：这个词指放射性碳，主要是碳十四。

branches.en: FROM AIR TO LIFE: atmospheric production and plant uptake connect sky to tissue.
branches.cn: 从空气到生命：大气生成与植物吸收把天空与组织连起来。

branches.en: MEASURED PORTION: a sample's residual amount is what a laboratory actually reads.
branches.cn: 被测部分：实验室真正读取的是样品中的残留量。

branches.en: DECAY CLOCK: the half-life turns the isotope into a timekeeper.
branches.cn: 衰变时钟：半衰期把同位素变成计时器。

branches.en: NAME FOR THE METHOD: metonymy lets the isotope stand for the technique.
branches.cn: 方法之名：转喻让同位素代指整套技术。

intro.en: Radiocarbon is a modern compound of a Latin ray prefix and a Latin charcoal noun, and both parts build a wide technical family.
intro.cn: radiocarbon 是近代复合词，由拉丁「射线」前缀与「炭」名词构成，两部分都构成大量技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius gives radio-, radium and radiograph; Latin carbo gives carbon, carbonate and carboniferous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 radius 产生 radio-、radium 与 radiograph；拉丁 carbo 产生 carbon、carbonate 与 carboniferous。

items.example: Radius is the source of the radio- prefix.
items.exampleCN: radius 是 radio- 前缀的来源。

items.structure: Latin radius, modern prefix for radiation
items.example: Radiocarbon uses radio- in its modern sense.
items.exampleCN: radiocarbon 用的是 radio- 的现代义。

items.example: Carbo named the element carbon.
items.exampleCN: carbo 命名了元素碳。

items.meaning: the element with atomic number six
items.example: Carbon forms the backbone of organic matter.
items.exampleCN: 碳构成有机物的骨架。

items.meaning: the radioactive isotope used for dating
items.meaningCN: 用于测年的放射性同位素碳十四
items.example: Carbon-14 decays into nitrogen-14.
items.exampleCN: 碳十四衰变为氮十四。

items.example: Radiocarbon enters plants through the air.
items.exampleCN: 放射性碳经空气进入植物。

items.example: Radiometric methods read decay.
items.exampleCN: 放射性测量方法读取衰变。

items.example: Radiogenic helium accumulates in rock.
items.exampleCN: 放射成因的氦在岩石中积累。

items.example: The radiocarbon age was about four thousand years.
items.exampleCN: 放射性碳年龄约为四千年。

definition_zh: 古代聚落；古代定居点
definition_en: a place where people lived together in the distant past, studied through its remains
core_image: 河谷台地上，一圈石墙围着十几座土坯房，中央有一口井，墙外是荒地
scene: 河谷台地上，一圈石墙围着十几座土坯房，中央有一口井。 A low stone wall enclosed the ancient settlement, and a well stood among a dozen mud-brick houses.
sceneCN: 这里 ancient settlement 指「古代人群长期共同居住的聚落」（第 1 个义项：古代聚落）；句意为低矮石墙围着一片古代聚落，十几座土坯房中间有一口井。可辨识物件：石墙、土坯房、水井、台地。

pos.zh: 古代聚落；古代定居点

senses.title: A settlement of the distant past
senses.definition: a place where a group lived together long ago, known mainly from its remains
senses.definitionCN: 很久以前一群人共同居住之处，主要凭遗存得知
senses.example: The ancient settlement stood on a terrace above the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古代聚落位于河流上方的台地上。
senses.why: The phrase joins an adjective of distance to a noun of dwelling, so it names a lived-in place known through remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示年代久远的形容词与表居住的名词连起来，指凭遗存得知的居住地。

senses.title: A prehistoric settlement
senses.definition: a settlement from before written records, dated by material remains
senses.definitionCN: 文字记录出现之前的聚落，靠物质遗存定年
senses.example: Huts and hearths mark the prehistoric ancient settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 茅屋与灶址标出了这处史前聚落。
senses.why: Where no texts exist, 'ancient' can reach back into prehistory, and the phrase carries no fixed date.
senses.whyCN: 在没有文字的地方，「古代」可以一直伸进史前，这个短语也不含固定年代界限。

senses.title: An early farming village
senses.definition: a village of the first farming communities, with houses, stores and fields
senses.definitionCN: 最初农业社群形成的村落，有房屋、粮仓与田地
senses.example: Grain pits show that the ancient settlement kept surplus seed.
senses.exampleCN: 粮坑说明这处古代聚落储存了余种。
senses.why: Farming tied people to one place, and the phrase often names the villages that resulted.
senses.whyCN: 农业把人绑在一处，这个短语常指由此形成的村落。

senses.title: A large settlement with urban features
senses.titleCN: 具有城市特征的较大聚落
senses.definition: a settlement large enough to have walls, planning or specialized quarters
senses.definitionCN: 大到拥有城墙、规划或专门区域的聚落
senses.example: The ancient settlement had a wall, a well and a row of workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 这处古代聚落有城墙、水井和一排作坊。
senses.why: Size and planning push the phrase from village toward town, though 'settlement' avoids claiming city status.
senses.whyCN: 规模与规划把这个短语从村落推向城镇，不过 settlement 一词避免了宣称城市地位。

senses.title: An archaeological site
senses.definition: the excavated or surveyed place treated as a unit of research
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究单元进行发掘或调查的地点
senses.example: The ancient settlement was mapped before any trench was opened.
senses.exampleCN: 在开挖探沟之前，这处古代聚落先做了测绘。
senses.why: Archaeology speaks of sites rather than towns because the legal and research unit is the place itself.
senses.whyCN: 考古学说「遗址」而不说「城镇」，因为法律与研究的单元就是这片地点本身。

senses.title: A chosen location for living
senses.definition: a place selected in the past for water, defence or trade, seen as a location
senses.definitionCN: 历史上因水源、防御或贸易而选定的地点
senses.example: The ancient settlement sits where two valleys meet.
senses.exampleCN: 这处古代聚落位于两条谷地交汇处。
senses.why: Location is part of the meaning: the phrase often explains why people built there.
senses.whyCN: 位置是词义的一部分：这个短语常用来说明人们为何在那里营建。

senses.title: The remains and layout of such a place
senses.titleCN: 古代聚落的遗存与布局
senses.definition: the houses, walls, paths and stores of such a place taken together
senses.definitionCN: 此类地点的房屋、墙体、道路与仓库的整体
senses.example: The ancient settlement's layout follows a single long street.
senses.exampleCN: 这处古代聚落的布局沿着一条长街展开。
senses.why: Once excavated, the phrase can name the whole arrangement rather than only the spot.
senses.whyCN: 发掘之后，这个短语可以指整套布局，而不只是那个地点。

senses.title: A long-established community in metaphor
senses.titleCN: 历史悠久、沿袭旧制的社区（比喻）
senses.definition: a living community described as if it were very old and set in its ways
senses.definitionCN: 被形容为年代久远、固守旧习的现实社区
senses.example: The firm behaves like an ancient settlement, jealous of newcomers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司行事像一座古代聚落，对新来者充满戒心。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows age, walls and suspicion of outsiders from the literal settlement.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从字面的聚落借来年岁、围墙与对外人的戒心。

intro.en: Ancient settlement joins a Latin-derived adjective of 'before' to an Old English noun of sitting down. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ancient settlement 把拉丁来源的「在前」形容词与古英语的「坐下安置」名词连在一起。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ante meant 'before, in front of'; the adjective for what belongs to former times was built on it.
items.cn: 拉丁 ante 意为「在前、在……之前」，指属于往昔的形容词即由它构成。

items.en: A spoken-Latin form reconstructed as anteanus 'belonging to before' stands behind Old French ancien.
items.cn: 一个被重构为 anteanus「属于以前的」的口语拉丁形式，是古法语 ancien 的前身。

items.en: Old English setl meant 'seat, sitting place'; the verb setlan 'to place, settle' came from it.
items.cn: 古英语 setl 意为「座位、坐处」；动词 setlan「安置、定居」即由此而来。

items.en: The noun ending -ment came from Latin -mentum through French, naming a result or an instrument.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ment 经法语来自拉丁 -mentum，指结果或工具。

items.en: English simply joins the two words; 'ancient settlement' is a descriptive label of modern archaeology, not an inherited phrase.
items.cn: 英语只是把两个词连起来；ancient settlement 是现代考古学的描述性标签，并非承袭的短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first use and reconstruction): the Vulgar Latin form anteanus is a reconstruction marked with an asterisk in etymological writing, and the phrase has no recorded first citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见使用与重构）：口语拉丁形式 anteanus 在词源写作中以星号标为重构；这个短语没有可考的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ancient or settlement but come from other stems; group two holds other names for places people lived in.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ancient、settlement 形近却另有词干的词；第二组是其他指人类居住处的名称。

entries.definition: From Latin antiquus 'former, old', a related but separate formation; it usually describes objects.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 antiquus「昔日的、旧的」，相关但另有构词；通常形容器物。

entries.definition: From Latin antecessor 'one who goes before', through French; it names a forebear, not a settlement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 antecessor「先行者」，经法语而来；指祖先，不是聚落。

entries.definition: From Latin sedimentum, based on sedere 'to sit'; it names material that has settled in water.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sedimentum，基于 sedere「坐」；指在水中沉积的物质。

entries.definition: Settle plus -er 'one who does'; it names a person who settles, not the place.
entries.definitionCN: settle 加 -er「做……的人」；指定居者，而非地点。

entries.definition: A small community and its houses, whether old or new.
entries.definitionCN: 小社群及其房屋，不论古今。

entries.definition: A very small group of houses, smaller than a village.
entries.definitionCN: 比村庄更小的几户人家。

entries.definition: A settlement planted by migrants, often with links to a parent state.
entries.definitionCN: 由移民建立、常与母国相连的聚落。

entries.definition: A place treated as an object of study, which may hold a settlement without being one.
entries.definitionCN: 作为研究对象的场所，可能含有聚落遗址却本身不等于聚落。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real word histories, the archaeological vocabulary and the mound image.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两条真实的词史、考古词汇，以及土丘意象。

normal.en: Ancient comes from Latin ante 'before' through Old French ancien.
normal.cn: ancient 来自拉丁 ante「在前」，经古法语 ancien。

normal.en: Settle comes from Old English setl 'seat' and setlan 'to place'.
normal.cn: settle 来自古英语 setl「座位」与 setlan「安置」。

normal.en: -ment is Latin -mentum, naming a result.
normal.cn: -ment 是拉丁 -mentum，指结果。

normal.en: Real terms: ancient settlement site, ancient settlement mound.
normal.cn: 真实术语：古代聚落遗址、古代聚落土丘。

normal.en: A settlement is a place, not a person; a settler is the person.
normal.cn: settlement 是地点，不是人；settler 才是人。

abstract.en: Picture a low wall around a dozen mud houses with one well at the centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一道矮墙围住十几座土坯房，中央一口井。

abstract.en: Picture a mound in a field that is all that remains of a busy street.
abstract.cn: 想象田野里一座土丘，那是一条热闹街道的全部残留。

abstract.en: Picture a firm with old walls and a gate that watches newcomers.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司有旧墙与一扇盯着新人的门。

examples.en: The ancient settlement was abandoned after the river changed course.
examples.cn: 河流改道后，这处古代聚落被废弃。

examples.en: Aerial survey revealed the plan of the ancient settlement.
examples.cn: 航拍调查显示了这处古代聚落的平面。

examples.en: The ancient settlement kept grain in pits lined with straw.
examples.cn: 这处古代聚落把谷物存放在铺草的坑里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ancient（古代）＋settlement（定居点）」——古代人住下来的地方 → 古代聚落

root: ancient 出拉丁 ante「在前」，经口语拉丁重构形式 anteanus 与古法语 ancien；settlement 出古英语 setl「座位」与 setlan「安置」，加拉丁 -mentum 经法语的名词词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a distant lived place to prehistoric and farming villages, larger planned settlements, archaeological sites, chosen locations, excavated layouts and a metaphor for an old community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从遥远的居住地出发，经过史前村落与农业村落、较大的规划聚落、考古遗址、选址、发掘后的布局，最后是旧社区的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled group of mud houses around one well on a river terrace.
core.cn: 核心意象：河谷台地上一圈土坯房围着一口井，外有矮墙。

branches.en: PLACE CHOSEN: a distant dwelling place is also a location chosen for water or defence.
branches.cn: 选定的地点：遥远的居住处同时也是因水源或防御而选的位置。

branches.en: FIRST LIVING: prehistory and early farming name the earliest forms of the place.
branches.cn: 最早的居住：史前与早期农业构成这处地点最早的形式。

branches.en: TOWNWARD: size and planning push the phrase beyond a mere village.
branches.cn: 向城而行：规模与规划把这个短语推过纯村落的界限。

branches.en: RESEARCH UNIT: the site and its excavated layout are archaeology's objects.
branches.cn: 研究单元：遗址及其发掘布局是考古学的对象。

branches.en: OLD WALLS: a living community borrows age and suspicion of outsiders.
branches.cn: 旧墙：现实社区借用了年岁与对外人的戒心。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin 'before' adjective with an Old English 'seat' noun and a Latin result suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁「在前」形容词、古英语「座位」名词与拉丁结果后缀合在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin ante gives ancient and ancestor; Old English setl gives settle, settlement and settler; Latin -mentum gives -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ante 产生 ancient 与 ancestor；古英语 setl 产生 settle、settlement 与 settler；拉丁 -mentum 产生 -ment。

items.example: Ante is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: ante 是这个形容词的基底。

items.example: The form is marked as a reconstruction.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式被标为重构。

items.example: The ancient wall still stands.
items.exampleCN: 古墙仍在。

items.example: Setl is the base of settle.
items.exampleCN: setl 是 settle 的基底。

items.example: The verb gave English settle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词产生英语 settle。

items.meaning: to make a home in a place
items.example: They settled beside the well.
items.exampleCN: 他们在井边定居。

items.example: Settlement uses this ending.
items.exampleCN: settlement 用了这个词尾。

items.meaning: a place or act of settling
items.example: The settlement grew along one street.
items.exampleCN: 聚落沿一条街扩展。

items.example: The first settlers dug the well.
items.exampleCN: 最早的定居者挖了那口井。

items.example: Ancestor shares the 'before' idea.
items.exampleCN: ancestor 共享「在前」之意。
