definition_zh: 社会结构；社会分层格局；群体间持久关系的总体安排；社会学中约束行动的格局
definition_en: the overall arrangement of institutions, roles and ranked groups that shapes how people in a society relate to one another
core_image: 一张摊开的村落地图，田块、祠堂、集市与水渠各归其位，人的位置被这些格子预先定好。
scene: 村口的地图钉在木板上，田块、祠堂、集市和水渠分列其上，谁在何处做事一目了然。 The social structure of the valley shows in its shared fields, shrines and market days.
sceneCN: 这里 social structure 指「一个社会中制度与角色的总体安排」（第 1 个义项：各类制度与角色被摆在一起的整体格局）；句意为这道山谷的社会结构体现在共耕的田、祠堂与赶集日之中。可辨识物件：钉在木板上的地图、田块、祠堂、集市摊位、水渠。

pos.zh: 社会结构；社会格局（可数，指某一社会的具体结构）

collocations.phrase: the social structure of a village

derivatives.zh: social + -ize（动词后缀）→ 由「社会的」转为「使社会化、与人交往」
society + -al（形容词后缀）→ 由「社会」转为「社会层面的」，比 social 更书面
structure + -al（拉丁形容词后缀）→ 由「结构」转为「结构上的」
structural + -ly（副词后缀）→ 由形容词转为副词，指从结构上看
structure + -ed（分词形容词后缀）→ 由「结构」转为「有结构的、安排有序的」

senses.title: The overall arrangement of institutions and roles
senses.titleCN: 制度与角色的总体安排
senses.definition: the way a society arranges its institutions, roles and positions taken together as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会把制度、角色与位置合在一起加以安排的方式
senses.example: The social structure of the valley shows in its shared fields, shrines and market days.
senses.exampleCN: 这道山谷的社会结构体现在共耕的田、祠堂与赶集日之中。
senses.why: structure is Latin structura, a building or arrangement, from struere 'to build up', so the phrase names the way a society is put together.
senses.whyCN: structure 是拉丁 structura，指建造或安排，出自 struere「堆叠建造」，因此这个短语指社会被搭起来的方式。

senses.title: The pattern of classes and ranks
senses.titleCN: 阶级与等级的分层格局
senses.definition: the ranking of people into classes or strata that stand above and below one another
senses.definitionCN: 把人排成一层层高于或低于彼此的阶级或阶层
senses.example: A mining town often keeps the social structure of the company that built it.
senses.exampleCN: 矿业城镇常保留着当初建镇公司的社会分层格局。
senses.why: building up is also building over: the same image describes layers stacked in order, so ranks become the visible form of the structure.
senses.whyCN: 往上建也是往上叠：同一意象用来描写按序堆叠的层，于是等级成了结构可见的形态。

senses.title: Lasting relations between groups
senses.definition: the durable pattern of links and exchanges that holds between families, professions or other groups
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、行业或其他群体之间稳定的联系与往来格局
senses.example: Trade marriages knit a social structure that outlives any single household.
senses.exampleCN: 联姻织成一种比任何单个家庭都活得久的社会结构。
senses.why: a structure holds its shape, so what the phrase singles out is the relation that persists rather than any one meeting.
senses.whyCN: 结构会保持形状，因此这个短语挑出的是持续存在的关系，而不是某一次会面。

senses.title: A society's frame
senses.definition: the frame within which a particular society carries on its ordinary life
senses.definitionCN: 某个具体社会在其中过日常生活的框架
senses.example: Each port town grew its own social structure around the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 每座港口城镇都在港湾周围长出自己的社会框架。
senses.why: the image of a frame says that the parts hold each other up, which is why one can speak of the structure of this society or that one.
senses.whyCN: 框架的意象说明各部分互相支撑，因此可以说这个社会的结构，也可以说那个社会的结构。

senses.title: A pattern that constrains what people can do
senses.titleCN: 社会学中约束行动的格局
senses.definition: in sociology, the recurring arrangement that limits and shapes what individuals are able to do
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中指反复出现、限制并塑造个人能做之事的安排
senses.example: The social structure decides who may speak at the assembly before anyone rises.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何人起身之前，社会结构就已经决定谁可以在会上发言。
senses.why: if the frame is built before the person arrives, it constrains the choices made inside it, which is the sociological reading of the word.
senses.whyCN: 如果框架在个人到来之前就已搭好，它就会约束其中作出的选择，这就是这个词的社会学读法。

senses.title: The internal shape of a group
senses.definition: the internal shape of a single group, such as a workshop, a school or a regiment
senses.definitionCN: 单个群体内部的结构，如作坊、学校或一团军队
senses.example: The workshop's social structure puts the oldest apprentice between the master and the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 作坊的社会结构把最年长的学徒放在师傅与其余人之间。
senses.why: the word scales down as easily as up: a small body of people is arranged in a shape just as a whole society is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词缩小与放大同样容易：一小群人和整个社会一样，也被安排成某种形状。

senses.title: A skeleton read apart from its filling
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：抽掉内容后剩下的骨架
senses.definition: the abstract skeleton of an arrangement, considered apart from the people who fill it
senses.definitionCN: 某种安排的抽象骨架，不考虑填在其中的具体人员
senses.example: The report describes the social structure of the firm and leaves out every name.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告描述公司的社会结构，却略去所有人名。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the load-bearing lines, the same way an engineer studies a frame without the walls.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留承重的那几条线，正如工程师研究框架时不管墙面。

senses.title: Relations that hold independently of individuals
senses.titleCN: 独立于具体个人而成立的关系
senses.definition: the relations between positions that keep their shape even when different people occupy them
senses.definitionCN: 位置之间的关系，即使换人来占据也保持原形
senses.example: The social structure of the guild survived every change of master.
senses.exampleCN: 行会的社会结构经受住了每一次师傅更替。
senses.why: once relations are detached from persons, the structure becomes a thing in its own right, and that is the most abstract reading.
senses.whyCN: 一旦关系与人脱开，结构本身就成了一件独立之物，这是最抽象的读法。

intro.en: Social comes from Latin socius 'companion, ally' plus -al, through French social. Structure comes from Latin structura 'a building, arrangement', from struere 'to build, pile up', through Old French. The compound is modern.
intro.cn: social 来自拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」加 -al，经法语 social 进入英语。structure 来自拉丁 structura「建筑、安排」，出自 struere「建造、堆叠」，经古法语传入。合成短语是近代产物。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、合伙人」。其更深来源不确定，有人为它提出的词根属重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Socialis 'of allies, of a community' was built on socius with the adjective suffix -alis; it described partnership before it described society at large.
items.cn: socialis「盟友的、共同体的」由 socius 加形容词后缀 -alis 构成；它先指伙伴关系，后指整个社会。

items.en: Struere meant 'to build, pile up, arrange'. It is generally regarded as going back to a root meaning 'to spread out in layers', but the Indo-European form given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: struere 意为「建造、堆叠、安排」。一般认为它可追溯到表示「分层铺开」的词根，但为其给出的印欧形式属重构形式。

items.en: Structura, from struere plus -ura, named the act and the result of building, hence a building or an arrangement of parts.
items.cn: structura 由 struere 加 -ura 构成，指建造的动作与结果，因此指建筑物或各部分的安排。

items.en: French social and Old French structure carried both words into English, first as adjectives and nouns of building, later of people.
items.cn: 法语 social 与古法语 structure 把这两个词带入英语，起初是形容词与建筑名词，后来才用于人。

items.en: Source uncertain: the compound social structure became a standard term only in modern sociology, no agreed first citation is recorded, and the pre-Latin shapes of socius and struere remain reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：social structure 直到近代社会学才成为标准术语，最早书证并无定说；socius 与 struere 在拉丁语之前的形式仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that share one element of the phrase and are easily confused with it; group two holds neighbouring concepts whose scope is different.
note.cn: 第一组是共享短语某一成分、容易与之混淆的词；第二组是范围不同的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The adjective for life among others, as in social life or social rules; alone it describes, while the phrase names the arrangement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与他人共同生活的形容词，如社交生活、社会规则；单独用时它在描写，短语则指安排本身。

entries.definition: Built on socius with -able, it describes a person who enjoys company; it is a temperament, not an arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 由 socius 加 -able 构成，形容喜欢与人相处的人；它指性情，不指安排。

entries.definition: From stringere 'to draw tight', it means a criticism or a narrowing, as in a stricture on trade; despite the similar shape it shares no root with structure.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 stringere「拉紧」，意为批评或限制，如对贸易的限制；尽管形状相似，它与 structure 并不同源。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts of anything, a building or a system; the full phrase restricts it to the arrangement of a society.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何事物的部分安排、建筑物或体系；完整短语把它限定为社会的安排。

entries.definition: The parts of a society seen as a working whole that keeps itself going; social structure stresses the shape, not the running.
entries.definitionCN: 把社会的各部分看作自行运转的整体；social structure 强调形状，而非运转。

entries.definition: The condition in which a society is peaceful and its rules are obeyed; structure can persist even through disorder.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会安宁、规则被遵守的状态；结构即使在动乱中也可以持续存在。

entries.definition: How people are grouped and how that grouping is run; social structure is the wider frame within which such grouping happens.
entries.definitionCN: 指人如何被编组以及编组如何被运作；social structure 是这种编组得以发生的更大框架。

entries.definition: One established body or practice, such as a school or a court; the social structure is the arrangement of many such parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个确立的机构或做法，如学校或法庭；social structure 是许多这类部分的总体安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: socius 'companion' plus -al: the adjective of living with others.
normal.cn: socius「同伴」加 -al：与人共同生活的形容词。

normal.en: struere 'to build up' plus -ura: the noun of what has been built.
normal.cn: struere「堆叠建造」加 -ura：指建成的那个东西的名词。

normal.en: The family runs social, societal, socialize, structure, structural, structured.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 social、societal、socialize、structure、structural、structured。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the angle: rigid social structure, change the social structure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角度：僵化的社会结构、改变社会结构。

normal.en: Sociology contrasts it with social system: the shape versus the running.
normal.cn: 社会学把它与 social system 对照：形状对运转。

abstract.en: Picture a building frame standing after every wall has been taken away.
abstract.cn: 想象一面面墙被拆走之后仍然立着的建筑骨架。

abstract.en: Picture seats in a hall that stay in their rows no matter who sits down.
abstract.cn: 想象礼堂里的座位，无论谁来坐都保持原来的排法。

abstract.en: Picture a village map where the well and the shrine decide where houses may stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张村落地图，水井与祠堂决定了房屋可以立在哪里。

examples.en: Industrialisation changed the social structure faster than any law could.
examples.cn: 工业化改变社会结构的速度快过任何法律。

examples.en: The novelist is more interested in the social structure of a kitchen than in its recipes.
examples.cn: 这位小说家更关心厨房里的社会结构，而不是菜谱。

examples.en: Fieldworkers map social structure by asking who borrows tools from whom.
examples.cn: 田野工作者通过询问谁向谁借工具来绘制社会结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（社交的）+ structure（构造）」——一群人的位置像房屋的梁柱一样被搭好 → 社会结构、分层格局

root: 拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」+ -al → social；拉丁 struere「建造、堆叠」→ structura「建筑、安排」→ structure。英语 social structure。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one frame: institutions and roles are raised into a whole, layers appear, relations hold between groups, the frame belongs to one society, it constrains action, it shrinks to a group, it is read as bare skeleton, and finally as relations that outlast their occupants.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一副框架展开：制度与角色被搭成整体，层次显现，群体之间维持关系，框架归属于某个社会，它约束行动，它可以缩小到一个团体，再被读作光秃的骨架，最后被读作比占据者更长久的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standing frame that gives every part its place before anyone enters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副立着的框架，在任何人进入之前就给每部分定好了位置。

branches.en: THE FRAME: institutions and roles, and the particular frame one society lives inside.
branches.cn: 框架：制度与角色，以及某个社会所处的那副具体框架。

branches.en: SHAPE AT TWO SCALES: ranks stacked in a society and the internal shape of a small group.
branches.cn: 两种尺度的形状：社会中堆叠的等级，与小团体内部的形状。

branches.en: HOLD AND LIMIT: durable links between groups are also the pattern that constrains action.
branches.cn: 维系与约束：群体之间持久的联系，同时也是约束行动的格局。

branches.en: BARE SKELETON: the arrangement read with every person left out.
branches.cn: 光秃的骨架：抽掉所有人之后读出的安排。

branches.en: DETACHED RELATIONS: positions keep their shape whoever fills them.
branches.cn: 脱开的关系：无论谁来占据，位置都保持原形。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase are Latin nouns enlarged by suffixes, and each half also lives on in a large English family.
intro.cn: 短语的两半都是经后缀扩大的拉丁名词，每一半也都在一个庞大的英语词族中延续。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius yields socialis and then social; Latin struere yields structura, and the two families meet in the modern compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 socialis，再衍生 social；拉丁 struere 衍生 structura；两个词族在近代合成短语中相遇。

items.structure: socius, socii (Latin noun, masculine, second declension)
items.example: The noun names a partner rather than a whole society.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指一个伙伴，而不是整个社会。

items.example: The adjective widened the partner word toward community life.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把「伙伴」的词扩展到共同体生活。

items.example: Socius plus -al gives the English adjective social.
items.exampleCN: socius 加 -al 得出英语形容词 social。

items.example: Societal pressure differs from the pressure of a single companion.
items.exampleCN: 整个社会的压力不同于单个同伴的压力。

items.structure: struere, struxi, structum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb names the act of laying one part on another.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把一部分叠在另一部分上的动作。

items.structure: structura, structurae (Latin noun, feminine, first declension)
items.example: Structura names the result of the building act.
items.exampleCN: structura 指建造动作的结果。

items.example: Struere plus -ura yields structura.
items.exampleCN: struere 加 -ura 得出 structura。

items.structure: structure (English noun, from Latin structura through French)
items.example: The bridge's structure was checked before the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨前检查了这座桥的结构。

items.example: Structural faults seldom show on the surface.
items.exampleCN: 结构性的缺陷很少显露在表面。

items.example: Sociology took social structure as one of its first objects.
items.exampleCN: 社会学把社会结构列为其最早的研究对象之一。

definition_zh: 社会网络；人际关系网；（在线）社交网络平台；某一群体内相互连接的关系总称
definition_en: the web of ties linking people to one another, or an online service through which users connect and share content
core_image: 一张纸上画满小圆点，点与点之间连着细线，线最密的地方人最多，孤零零的点只有一条线
scene: 研究者把村里谁帮过谁逐一记下，再把名字用线连起来，纸上渐渐显出一片网。 The team mapped the social network of the village by recording who helped whom.
sceneCN: 研究者把村里谁帮过谁逐一记录，再用线把名字连起来，纸上渐渐显出一片网；句中的 social network 指「由人际关系连成的整体网络」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间实际往来所构成的关系网）。图中可辨识物件：手绘的关系图、连线的名字卡、村落地图。

pos.zh: 社会网络；人际关系网；社交平台（可数短语名词）

derivatives.zh: 社交网络活动；通过网络建立关系（短语后加表示「活动、过程」的后缀，由静态的网转为持续的交往行为）
建立人脉；联网（由「网」这一名词加表示过程的后缀，指把关系或设备连起来这件事）
在社会方面；在社交上（加副词后缀，把「社会的」转为修饰行为方式）
交往；使社会化（加表示「使成为」的动词后缀，由「社会的」转为进入社会关系的过程）
联网的；连成网络的（加过去分词后缀，表示已被连入网中）

senses.title: The web of personal ties
senses.titleCN: 由实际往来连成的人际关系网
senses.definition: the set of relationships that link a person to relatives, friends, neighbours and colleagues
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人与亲戚、朋友、邻居和同事连接起来的那些关系的总和
senses.example: Most jobs in the village were found through the social network rather than through advertisements.
senses.exampleCN: 村里大多数工作是通过人际关系网找到的，而不是通过广告。
senses.why: the phrase joins a word for companionship to a word for a mesh of threads, so the literal picture is people held together by lines of contact.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示「同伴」的词与表示「线网」的词连在一起，字面画面就是人被一条条往来之线系在一起。

senses.title: A structure that can be measured
senses.titleCN: 可作为结构测量的社会网络
senses.definition: the pattern of ties in a group, studied as nodes and links with measurable density and reach
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中连线的格局，以节点与连线来研究，其密度与覆盖范围都可测量
senses.example: Research using social network analysis showed that two brokers connected the two halves of the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 运用社会网络分析的研究显示，两名中间人把公司的两半连接了起来。
senses.why: sociology turned the everyday web into an object of measurement: once ties are drawn as lines between points, questions of distance and clustering can be asked.
senses.whyCN: 社会学把日常的关系网变成可测量的对象：一旦把往来画成点与点之间的线，距离与聚集程度就可以提问了。

senses.title: An online platform of connections
senses.definition: a website or application on which users create profiles and link to one another
senses.definitionCN: 用户在其中建立个人页面并互相连接的网站或应用
senses.example: The campaign reached younger voters mainly through a social network.
senses.exampleCN: 这场竞选活动主要通过一个社交平台接触到年轻选民。
senses.why: the digital sense keeps the old image and changes only the medium: the lines are now drawn by clicks rather than by visits.
senses.whyCN: 数字义保留旧的意象，只换了媒介：线不再由走动画出，而由点击画出。

senses.title: Relationships as usable capital
senses.definition: the contacts a person can call on for advice, introductions or favours
senses.definitionCN: 一个人可以求取建议、引荐或帮忙的那些联系人
senses.example: She spent her first year in the city building a social network she could rely on.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这座城市的第一年都在经营一张可以依靠的人脉网。
senses.why: because a network can be drawn on, English uses it for advantage: the tie is not only a description of closeness but a resource that can be spent.
senses.whyCN: 由于网可以被取用，英语便用它来表示优势：连线不只是亲疏的描述，也是可以花掉的资源。

senses.title: The path along which news travels
senses.titleCN: 信息借以扩散的传播路径
senses.definition: the routes through which information, rumour or behaviour passes from person to person
senses.definitionCN: 信息、传言或行为从一个人传到另一个人的那些路径
senses.example: A rumour moves faster through a dense social network than through scattered strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 传言在稠密的社会网络中比在分散的陌生人之间传得更快。
senses.why: a mesh is also a channel: whatever is placed on one thread can travel along the threads that touch it.
senses.whyCN: 网同时也是通道：放在某一根线上的东西，可以沿着与它相接的线传开。

senses.title: Kin and mutual aid
senses.titleCN: 人类学中的亲属与互助网络
senses.definition: the ties of marriage, descent and reciprocal help that hold a community together
senses.definitionCN: 由婚姻、血缘与互相帮助构成、把一个社群维系在一起的连线
senses.example: Anthropologists traced the social network that decided who would harvest whose field.
senses.exampleCN: 人类学家追踪了那张决定谁帮谁收割的社会网络。
senses.why: in small communities the web is often the whole economy: obligations run along kin lines, and the diagram explains who owes what.
senses.whyCN: 在小社群里，这张网常常就是全部经济：义务沿着亲属连线运行，图一画出来，谁欠谁一目了然。

senses.title: Customers linked by talk
senses.titleCN: 由口碑相连的顾客网络
senses.definition: the web of customer relationships along which recommendations and complaints spread
senses.definitionCN: 顾客之间的关系网，推荐与抱怨沿着它传播
senses.example: The brand grew because its social network of users recommended it without being paid.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌之所以成长，是因为它的用户网络在无偿地为它推荐。
senses.why: marketing borrowed the term for the same reason sociology did: word of mouth follows existing ties, not random contact.
senses.whyCN: 营销学借这个词的理由与社会学相同：口碑沿着既有的连线走，而不走随机的接触。

senses.title: Ties among animals
senses.titleCN: 行为生态学中的动物社会网络
senses.definition: the pattern of repeated associations among animals of the same population
senses.definitionCN: 同一动物群体中个体之间反复结伴所形成的格局
senses.example: Biologists mapped the social network of the troop by noting every grooming pair.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家记录下每一对互相理毛的个体，从而绘出这个族群的社会网络。
senses.why: the phrase was extended to any population whose members recognize and repeatedly meet one another, because the geometry of ties is the same.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语被扩展到任何成员彼此识别并反复相遇的群体，因为连线的几何形状是一样的。

intro.en: Social network is a two-part phrase with two very different histories. Social comes from Latin socius 'companion, ally' through the adjective socialis. Network is a native English compound of net and work, both Old English words, and has no Latin source. The phrase as a term of sociology took shape in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: social network 是由两部分组成的短语，两部分的来历很不相同。social 经拉丁形容词 socialis 出自拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」；network 是英语本族复合词，由 net 与 work 两个古英语词构成，并无拉丁来源。这个短语作为社会学术语在二十世纪成形。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to the Latin verb for following is sometimes suggested but remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、伙伴」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出它与表示「跟随」的拉丁动词有关，但那仍是假说。

items.en: The adjective socialis 'of a companion, allied, sociable' was formed with the adjective suffix -alis, and it supplied the English word social.
items.cn: 形容词 socialis「同伴的、结盟的、好交际的」由形容词性后缀 -alis 构成，英语的 social 即由此而来。

items.en: Net is a native word for a mesh of cords with openings, recorded in Old English and going back to a reconstructed Germanic form; it is not related to Latin.
items.cn: net 是英语本族词，指带孔洞的绳网，古英语已有记录，可追溯到日耳曼语的重构形式；它与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Weorc meant 'work, deed, something made'. Net and weorc were joined in English to name a woven mesh of threads, and later any interconnected system.
items.cn: weorc 意为「工作、作为、做成之物」。net 与 weorc 在英语中结合，先指编成的线网，后来指任何彼此连接的系统。

items.en: By the twentieth century the compound network was applied to railways, telephones and then to people, and social network became the standard phrase for a web of human ties.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，复合词 network 先后用于铁路、电话，再用于人，social network 于是成为表示人际关系网的标准说法。

items.en: The phrase was fixed as a sociological term in the 1950s, and the online sense followed in the 2000s. Source note: the Latin noun for companion has an uncertain deeper origin, and every form proposed for the Germanic net is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 这个短语在二十世纪五十年代固定为社会学用语，在线义则在二十一世纪初出现。来源说明：拉丁语中表示同伴的名词其更深来源不确定，为日耳曼语 net 提出的形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same phrase and its close compounds, which are constantly confused; group two holds neighbouring ideas, each naming a different part of the same picture.
note.cn: 第一组是同一短语的各种形式与近邻复合词，极易混淆；第二组是相邻概念，各自指同一幅画面中的不同部分。

entries.definition: Names the activity of building and using ties, especially online; the plain phrase names the web itself, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立并使用关系的活动，尤指在线进行；原短语指这张网本身，而不是这件事。

entries.definition: Names the platforms and published content; a social network is the pattern of connections those platforms make visible.
entries.definitionCN: 指平台与发布的内容；social network 则是这些平台使之可见的连接格局。

entries.definition: The general word for any interconnected system, from railways to computers; it says nothing about people unless social is attached.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何互联系统，从铁路到计算机；若不加上 social，便与人无关。

entries.definition: The practical activity of making professional contacts, often at events; it is narrower and more purposeful than a whole social network.
entries.definitionCN: 指在活动中建立职业联系的实际行为；它比整张社会网络更窄、更有目的性。

entries.definition: A group defined by place, interest or identity; a social network is defined by the ties themselves, which may cross community borders.
entries.definitionCN: 由地点、兴趣或身份界定的群体；社会网络则由连线本身界定，可以跨越社群边界。

entries.definition: The advantage a person gains from having ties; it is the yield of the network, not the network's shape.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人因拥有连线而获得的优势；它是网络的产出，而非网络的形状。

entries.definition: The people one regularly meets socially; it is a small, personal ring rather than a mapped structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人日常交往的那群人；它是小型的私人圈子，而非被绘出的结构。

entries.definition: A web formed only by descent and marriage; the broader social network also includes friendship, work and exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 仅由血缘与婚姻构成的网；更广义的社会网络还包括友谊、工作与交换关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin half, the native English half and the real research settings in which the phrase is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自这个短语真实的拉丁语一半、英语本族一半，以及它真正出现的研究场景。

normal.en: Half the phrase is Latin 'companion', half is Old English 'net' plus 'work': a mesh made of companions.
normal.cn: 短语的一半是拉丁语的「同伴」，另一半是古英语的「网」加「做工」：由同伴编成的网。

normal.en: The family runs social, socially, socialize, networking, networked.
normal.cn: 词族包括 social、socially、socialize、networking、networked。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the research setting: social network analysis, social network ties, social network theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出研究场景：社会网络分析、社会网络纽带、社会网络理论。

normal.en: The diagram is the mnemonic: dots are people, lines are contact, dense patches are where influence travels.
normal.cn: 图本身就是记忆线索：点是人物，线是往来，线密处正是影响力流动的地方。

normal.en: Digital use changes the medium, not the picture: profiles and follows are dots and lines again.
normal.cn: 数字化只换媒介，不换画面：主页与关注仍然是点与线。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose planks are names, each plank held by the two beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，桥板是一个个名字，每块板都由左右两块托住。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour crossing a courtyard from window to window without ever entering the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言从一个窗口传到另一个窗口，穿过整个院子，却始终没有走到街上。

abstract.en: Picture a single dot at the edge of the page with only one line leaving it, and everyone knows whom it relies on.
abstract.cn: 想象纸边一个孤点只伸出一条线，所有人都知道它靠的是谁。

examples.en: A longitudinal study found that a sparse social network predicted loneliness better than income did.
examples.cn: 一项追踪研究发现，稀疏的社会网络比收入更能预测孤独感。

examples.en: The firm's growth depended on a social network of suppliers who vouched for one another.
examples.cn: 这家公司的成长依赖于一张供应商彼此担保的社会网络。

examples.en: She left the platform but kept the social network it had given her.
examples.cn: 她离开了那个平台，却留下了平台给她的那张人脉网。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆作「social（社会的）+ network（网）」——把认识的人用线连成一张网，网上既是关系也是平台 → 社会网络、人脉、社交网站。

root: social：拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」→ 形容词 socialis（加 -alis）→ 英语 social；network：古英语 net「网」+ weorc「工作、做成之物」构成英语本族复合词，非拉丁来源 → 二十世纪社会学中固定为 social network。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a drawn web of personal ties becomes a measurable structure, then a platform that redraws it, a resource to spend, a channel for news, a kin-based support system, a market of talk, and finally the same geometry among animals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：一张被画出的人际网先成为可测量的结构，再成为重新绘制它的平台、可以花掉的资源、新闻的通道、以亲属为骨架的互助体系、由口碑构成的市场，最后落到动物之间同样的几何形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: names placed as dots on paper and joined by lines, so that closeness becomes a visible distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：把名字当作纸上的点，再用线连起来，亲疏于是变成可见的距离。

branches.en: FROM LIFE TO DIAGRAM: real visits first form the web, and method then turns that web into nodes, links and density.
branches.cn: 从生活到图纸：真实走动先织成网，方法再把这张网变成节点、连线与密度。

branches.en: MEDIUM AND ADVANTAGE: the platform redraws the lines by clicks, and those lines become capital that can be called upon.
branches.cn: 媒介与优势：平台用点击重新画线，而这些线又成为可以调用的资本。

branches.en: FLOW AND SUPPORT: the mesh carries news along its threads, and along kin threads it carries help and obligation.
branches.cn: 流动与支撑：网沿着线运送消息，也沿着亲属线运送帮助与义务。

branches.en: MARKET: talk about a product follows the same threads, so the network doubles as a sales channel.
branches.cn: 市场：关于产品的谈论沿着同样的线走，于是这张网同时成为销售渠道。

branches.en: OTHER SPECIES: the geometry is unchanged when the dots are animals that groom, hunt or travel together.
branches.cn: 其他物种：当点是互相理毛、一同捕猎或迁徙的动物时，几何形状并未改变。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 经 socialis 与形容词后缀 -alis 提供「社会」这一半；「网」这一半来自古英语的 net 与 weorc，背后并没有拉丁词形。

definition_zh: 社会转型；社会结构、制度与生活方式发生的深层整体变化
definition_en: a deep and wide change in the structure, institutions or daily life of a society

senses.title: Structural change of a society
senses.definition: a deep change in the way a society is organised, including its classes, work and families
senses.definitionCN: 社会组织的深层变化，包括阶层、工作与家庭
senses.example: The fishing town underwent a social transformation after the new port opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新港口开通后，这座渔镇经历了社会转型。
senses.why: Transformation is a change of form, so the phrase points to a new shape of society rather than a single new law.
senses.whyCN: transformation 是形态的改变，因此这个短语指向社会的新形态，而非某一条新法律。

senses.title: Institutional transformation
senses.definition: a change in the rules, organisations and offices that govern a society
senses.definitionCN: 治理社会的规则、组织与机构发生变化
senses.example: Land reform was the first step in the country's social transformation.
senses.exampleCN: 土地改革是这个国家社会转型的第一步。
senses.why: Institutions are the skeleton of society; when they are rebuilt, the change outlasts any single government.
senses.whyCN: 制度是社会的骨架；骨架重建后，变化会比任何一届政府都长久。

senses.title: Industrial and urban transformation
senses.titleCN: 工业化与城市化驱动的转型
senses.definition: the reshaping of work and settlement that follows industry and urban growth
senses.definitionCN: 随工业与城市增长而来的工作与居住形态重塑
senses.example: Industrialisation drove a social transformation that moved families from fields to factories.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化推动了一场社会转型，把家庭从田地移向工厂。
senses.why: Machines and cities are the usual engines: they change where people live and what they do.
senses.whyCN: 机器与城市是常见引擎：它们改变人住在哪里、做什么。

senses.title: Change in values and daily life
senses.titleCN: 价值与日常生活的变化
senses.definition: a shift in beliefs, habits and expectations about family, work and status
senses.definitionCN: 关于家庭、工作与地位的信念、习惯与期待发生转变
senses.example: The social transformation showed first in smaller households and later marriages.
senses.exampleCN: 这场社会转型最先表现在家庭变小与晚婚上。
senses.why: Numbers and habits are where deep change becomes visible, long before any constitution is rewritten.
senses.whyCN: 数字与习惯是深层变化显现之处，远早于宪法被改写。

senses.title: A planned programme of change
senses.definition: a deliberate campaign by a state or movement to remake society
senses.definitionCN: 国家或运动有意识地重塑社会
senses.example: The literacy campaign was part of a wider social transformation.
senses.exampleCN: 扫盲运动是更广泛社会转型的一部分。
senses.why: The phrase can name a project with agents and targets, not only an unplanned drift.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以指有推动者与目标的项目，而不只是无意的漂移。

senses.title: Digital transformation of social life
senses.titleCN: 社会生活的数字化转型
senses.definition: the reshaping of communication, work and services by digital networks
senses.definitionCN: 数字网络对通信、工作与服务的重塑
senses.example: Mobile payment brought a quiet social transformation to market stalls.
senses.exampleCN: 移动支付给菜市场带来一场安静的社会转型。
senses.why: Each technology wave produces its own version of the phrase, and digital networks are the current one.
senses.whyCN: 每一波技术都会产生自己版本的这一短语，数字网络是当前的一版。

senses.title: Dislocation and unequal costs
senses.definition: the disruption and uneven burdens that accompany deep change
senses.definitionCN: 深层变化伴随的失序与不均衡负担
senses.example: The social transformation enriched the coast while emptying the inland villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这场社会转型让沿海富裕，却让内陆村庄空心化。
senses.why: Deep change redistributes not only benefits but also losses, and the phrase often carries that ledger.
senses.whyCN: 深层变化不只重新分配收益，也分配损失，这个短语常带着这本账。

senses.title: Shift from one social form to another
senses.titleCN: 从一种社会形态转到另一种
senses.definition: the abstract passage of a society from one organised form to another
senses.definitionCN: 社会从一种组织形态过渡到另一种
senses.example: Historians describe the social transformation as a change of form, not a change of fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这场社会转型描述为形态的改变，而非风尚的改变。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the Latin image of form: a society is reshaped, as clay is reshaped.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留拉丁「形状」的意象：社会被重新塑造，如同黏土被重新塑形。

intro.en: Social transformation joins social, from Latin socius 'companion, ally', with transformation, from Late Latin transformatio, built on trans- 'across' and forma 'shape'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social transformation 由 social 与 transformation 合成：social 来自拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」；transformation 来自晚期拉丁 transformatio，由 trans-「越过」与 forma「形状」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. It is generally connected with sequi 'to follow', but that link is a hypothesis and the pre-Latin form is reconstructed.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、伙伴」。一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关，但这一联系只是假说，拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式。

items.en: Forma meant 'shape, form, mould'. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: forma 意为「形状、形态、模子」。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Trans- 'across' plus forma produced transformare 'to change the shape of', and the noun transformatio named the change.
items.cn: trans-「越过」加 forma 构成 transformare「改变形状」，名词 transformatio 指这种改变。

items.en: English transformation entered in the fourteenth century through French, first as a change of form or appearance.
items.cn: 英语 transformation 在十四世纪经法语进入，最初指形状或外观的改变。

items.en: Social science applied the phrase to deep structural change in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, often alongside industrialisation.
items.cn: 社会科学在十九与二十世纪把这个短语用于深层结构变化，常与工业化并提。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first use of the exact phrase is not fixed, and the link of socius to sequi is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个确切短语的最早使用无法确定；socius 与 sequi 的联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one shares the two stems; group two holds other names for societies changing.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词干；第二组是用其他名称表达社会变化。

entries.definition: Relating to society; it marks the field, not the change.
entries.definitionCN: 与社会相关；标记领域，而非变化。

entries.definition: The organised group itself; transformation is what happens to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指组织起来的群体本身；转型是它经历的事。

entries.definition: A change of form in anything; the phrase narrows it to society.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何事物的形态变化；短语把它限定到社会。

entries.definition: To change the form of something; it can be used of clay, data or a society.
entries.definitionCN: 指改变某物的形态；可用于黏土、数据或社会。

entries.definition: Any alteration in social life; transformation stresses depth and a new shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会生活中的任何改变；转型强调深度与新形态。

entries.definition: The passage from one state to another, often without implying a better end.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一种状态过渡到另一种，常不暗示更好的终点。

entries.definition: A deliberate improvement of institutions, usually within the existing form.
entries.definitionCN: 指对制度的有意改良，通常在既有形态内进行。

entries.definition: A specific historical direction of change, while transformation can go in any direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个特定的历史变化方向，而转型可以朝任何方向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real contrasts, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实对比，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Trans- is across and forma is shape: a transformation is a change of shape.
normal.cn: trans- 是越过，forma 是形状：transformation 就是形状的改变。

normal.en: The family runs social, society, socially, transform, transformation, transformative.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 social、society、socially、transform、transformation、transformative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rapid social transformation, undergo social transformation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：快速的社会转型、经历社会转型。

normal.en: Distinguish it from social change: change is any alteration, transformation is deep and structural.
normal.cn: 与 social change 区分：change 是任何改变，transformation 是深层结构性的。

normal.en: The phrase often appears with industry, ports, cities and generations.
normal.cn: 这个短语常与工业、港口、城市与代际连用。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of one town laid on top of each other.
abstract.cn: 想象同一座城镇的两张地图叠在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour where fishing boats give way to container cranes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个港口，渔船让位给集装箱吊机。

abstract.en: Picture clay being pressed into a new mould and keeping the fingerprints.
abstract.cn: 想象黏土被压进新模子，却留下指纹。

examples.en: The social transformation of the valley began with a road and ended with a new generation.
examples.cn: 这个山谷的社会转型始于一条路，终于新一代人。

examples.en: Economists measure social transformation by employment, education and household size.
examples.cn: 经济学家用就业、教育与家庭规模衡量社会转型。

examples.en: A social transformation can be welcomed and resisted in the same town.
examples.cn: 同一座城镇里，社会转型可以同时被欢迎与被抵制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（社会的）+ transformation（变形）」——整个社会换了一副骨架

root: social 来自拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」，一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关，但属假说；transformation 来自晚期拉丁 transformatio = trans-（越过）+ forma（形状）。更早形态均为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reshaping: structures change, institutions are rebuilt, industry and cities move people, values shift, programmes are launched, digital networks spread, costs are unevenly borne, and the society ends in a new form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次重塑展开：结构改变，制度重建，工业与城市迁移人口，价值转变，改造项目启动，数字网络铺开，代价分配不均，社会最终呈现新形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two maps of one town laid on top of each other, with harbour, factories and homes all moved.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座城镇的两张地图叠在一起，港口、工厂与住宅都换了位置。

branches.en: FORM ITSELF: deep change is a new shape, not a new fashion.
branches.cn: 形态本身：深层变化是新形状，而非新风尚。

branches.en: SKELETON: institutions are rebuilt and outlast governments.
branches.cn: 骨架：制度被重建，且比政府更长久。

branches.en: ENGINES: industry, cities and digital networks each move people and work.
branches.cn: 引擎：工业、城市与数字网络各自迁移人口与工作。

branches.en: DAILY LIFE: households and marriages show the change before documents do.
branches.cn: 日常生活：家庭与婚姻比文件更早显现变化。

branches.en: PLAN AND LEDGER: a campaign can drive change, and the losses are distributed unevenly.
branches.cn: 计划与账本：运动可以推动变化，损失却分配不均。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius supplies social, society and associate; Latin forma supplies form, format and transformation, with trans- adding the change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 social、society 与 associate；拉丁 forma 衍生 form、format 与 transformation，trans- 增添变化。

senses.definition: of the harvest time or the ripening of crops and fruit
senses.definitionCN: 指收获时节或庄稼、果实的成熟
senses.example: Autumnal orchards hung heavy with late apples.
senses.exampleCN: 秋日的果园挂满晚熟的苹果，沉甸甸的。
senses.why: Autumn was the Roman harvest season, so the word keeps the ripeness within it.
senses.whyCN: 秋天本是罗马的收获季，这个词里始终藏着「成熟」。

senses.title: Of the year's later months
senses.definition: of the later part of the year, especially September to November
senses.definitionCN: 指一年较晚的时段，尤其是九至十一月
senses.example: An autumnal chill settled over the village.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵秋寒笼罩了村庄。
senses.why: Calendars divide the year, and the adjective marks the third quarter.
senses.whyCN: 历法把一年分段，这个形容词标出第三季。

senses.title: Past the prime of life
senses.definition: of a person or career, past the peak, in a later phase
senses.definitionCN: 指人或事业已过巅峰、处于后段
senses.example: The poet's autumnal works are gentler than his early verses.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人晚期的作品比早年诗行更为温缓。
senses.why: The year becomes a life: spring is youth, autumn is the wise decline.
senses.whyCN: 一年即一生：春为青春，秋为渐老中的从容。

senses.title: Melancholy and wistful
senses.definition: of a mood, tinged with gentle sadness, like fading leaves
senses.definitionCN: （心境）带淡淡哀愁，如落叶般怅然
senses.example: There was something autumnal in her farewell letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她的告别信里透着一股秋意般的惆怅。
senses.why: Falling leaves and shortening days teach a soft melancholy; the word absorbed it.
senses.whyCN: 落叶与渐短的白昼教会人淡淡的哀愁，这个词把这份哀愁吸了进去。

senses.title: Of warm colors
senses.definition: of the orange, red, and brown colors of the season
senses.definitionCN: 指橙、红、褐等秋天特有的色彩
senses.example: She chose autumnal shades for the dining room.
senses.exampleCN: 她为餐厅挑了秋色的暖调。
senses.why: Design borrows the season's palette, and the adjective names it.
senses.whyCN: 设计界借用季节的调色盘，这个形容词为其命名。

senses.title: In astronomy and the calendar
senses.definition: of celestial events occurring in or named for autumn, as the autumnal equinox
senses.definitionCN: 指发生在秋季或以秋季命名的事件，如秋分
senses.example: The autumnal equinox marks the sun's crossing southward.
senses.exampleCN: 秋分标志着太阳南移越过赤道。
senses.why: Science needed a formal adjective for the season's celestial markers.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个正式形容词来指称秋季的天文节点。

senses.title: Of late flourishing before an end
senses.definition: of a late period of activity or beauty just before an ending
senses.definitionCN: 指终结之前最后的活跃或盛放
senses.example: The band's autumnal reunion tour was its most graceful.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队晚期的重组巡演最为从容优雅。
senses.why: Autumn holds both ripeness and decline, so the word fits final glories.
senses.whyCN: 秋天同时承载成熟与凋零，这个词因此适用于迟来的辉煌。

intro.en: Autumnal comes from Latin autumnalis, formed on autumnus, the season of harvest; the older history of autumnus itself is uncertain, possibly Etruscan. English formed the adjective in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: autumnal 出自拉丁语 autumnalis，其基础是收获季一词 autumnus；autumnus 更早的来源不确定，或出自伊特鲁里亚语。英语形容词形成于 17 世纪。

items.en: The further source of autumnus is unknown; an Etruscan origin has been proposed but not proven.
items.cn: autumnus 的更早来源不明；有伊特鲁里亚语起源说，但未被证实。

items.en: autumnus named the harvest season, the time of ripening crops and vintage.
items.cn: 拉丁语 autumnus 指收获之季，即庄稼成熟、葡萄采收的时节。

items.en: autumnalis was the formal adjective, of or belonging to autumn.
items.cn: autumnalis 是正式形容词，意为「属于秋天的」。

items.en: The season word passed through Old French autompne into Middle English autumpne.
items.cn: 季节词经古法语 autompne 进入中古英语 autumpne。

items.en: English simplified the noun to autumn by the sixteenth century, displacing the native harvest.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪英语将名词简化为 autumn，取代了本族的 harvest 一词。

items.en: The adjective autumnal formed in the seventeenth century and quickly grew its moods and metaphors.
items.cn: 形容词 autumnal 形成于 17 世纪，很快长出各类心绪与比喻义。

note.cn: 第一组收季节词族及形近词；第二组收四季形容词与相关心绪词。

entries.definitionCN: 春天的，出自拉丁语 vernalis；autumnal 的对位词。

entries.definition: of winter, from Latin hibernalis.
entries.definitionCN: 冬天的，出自拉丁语 hibernalis。

entries.definitionCN: 自给自足的，出自希腊语 autos + arkein；仅开头读音相似，词源无关。

entries.definitionCN: 黄褐色的，出自法语 tanné「鞣制的」；词源与季节无关。

entries.definition: the American name for the season, from the fall of leaves.
entries.definitionCN: 美式对秋季的称呼，源自「落叶」之意。

entries.definition: reddish-brown, the color of autumn leaves and apples.
entries.definitionCN: 红褐色的；秋叶与秋果的颜色。

entries.definition: gentle sadness; the mood autumnal often carries.
entries.definitionCN: 忧郁；autumnal 常带的心绪。

entries.definition: soft, rich, and ripe, like autumn light or late fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 醇熟的；柔和丰厚的，如秋光与晚果。

entries.definition: past the peak and moving toward the end.
entries.definitionCN: 衰落的；已过巅峰、走向尾声的。

normalIntro.en: autumnal is autumn plus the Latin adjective ending: the season turned into a quality.
normalIntro.cn: autumnal 即 autumn 加拉丁形容词词尾：把季节化成一种质地。

normal.en: autumn + al: keep the silent n, unlike the noun's spelling tricks.
normal.cn: autumn + al：保留不发音的 n，注意拼写变化。

normal.en: The season-adjective set: vernal, estival, autumnal, hibernal.
normal.cn: 四季形容词一组记：vernal、estival、autumnal、hibernal。

normal.en: autumnal equinox is the set astronomical phrase.
normal.cn: autumnal equinox 是天文学固定说法：秋分。

normal.en: Figuratively: autumnal years are the years past summer's prime.
normal.cn: 比喻用法：autumnal years 即过了盛夏的人生晚境。

normal.en: Its mood is mellow, not bitter: gentle sadness like falling leaves.
normal.cn: 它的心绪是醇而非苦：如落叶般的淡淡哀愁。

abstract.en: Picture late light lying low across a stubble field.
abstract.cn: 想象低斜的秋光铺在收割后的田茬上。

abstract.en: The word smells of woodsmoke and ripe pears.
abstract.cn: 这个词闻起来有烟柴与熟梨的气息。

abstract.en: Autumnal is summer's echo growing golden and quiet.
abstract.cn: autumnal 是夏天的回声，渐渐变金、归于安静。

examples.en: The lake turned autumnal gold by the third week of October.
examples.cn: 到十月第三周，湖面已是一片秋金。

examples.en: In his autumnal years the general wrote memoirs instead of orders.
examples.cn: 晚年时分，将军写的是回忆录，不再是作战命令。

examples.en: There was an autumnal hush in the empty school corridor.
examples.cn: 空荡的学校走廊里有一种秋日般的沉静。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the season outward: the calendar autumn, the harvest, the late years of a life, the gentle melancholy, and the colors named after falling leaves.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随季节向外延展：历法之秋、收获之秋、人生之晚境、淡淡的惆怅，以及以落叶命名的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: golden light over ripening fields, leaves about to fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：金色秋光铺在渐熟的田野上，落叶将坠未坠。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR SIDE: the equinox and the year's third quarter.
branches.cn: 历法一面：秋分与一年的第三季。

branches.en: THE RIPE SIDE: harvest fruit and the season's warm palette.
branches.cn: 成熟一面：收获的果实与季节的暖调色。

branches.en: THE LIFE SIDE: late years and late glories.
branches.cn: 人生一面：晚境与迟来的辉煌。

branches.en: THE MOOD SIDE: melancholy like falling leaves.
branches.cn: 心绪一面：如落叶般的惆怅。

branches.en: THE FINAL SIDE: one last flourishing before the end.
branches.cn: 尾声一面：终结前最后的盛放。

intro.en: autumnal is autumnus plus -al, the standard Latin adjective ending; the season stem stays visible throughout.
intro.cn: autumnal 由 autumnus 加 -al 构成，后者是拉丁语标准形容词词尾；季节词干贯穿全词。

latinIntro.en: Latin built four season adjectives in -alis: vernalis, aestivus, autumnalis, hibernalis; English borrowed them all.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 -alis 造了四个季节形容词：vernalis、aestivus、autumnalis、hibernalis——英语全部借入。

senses.title: The recluse in the hills
senses.definition: a person who has withdrawn from society under a vow or for ascetic reasons
senses.definitionCN: 因誓愿或苦修而退出社会的人
senses.example: The recluse in the hills had not left his valley in years.
senses.exampleCN: 山中的那位隐士已经多年没有离开山谷。
senses.why: The first sense carries a purpose: the withdrawal is chosen and disciplined.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项带着目的：退隐是主动的、有戒律的。

senses.title: A recluse by temperament
senses.definition: someone who avoids company because other people have become hard to bear
senses.definitionCN: 因为难以忍受他人而回避交往的人
senses.example: After the trial she became a recluse in her own city.
senses.exampleCN: 那场审判之后，她成了自己城市里的避世者。
senses.why: Here the cause is injury or exhaustion, not a vow.
senses.whyCN: 这里的起因是受伤或疲惫，而不是誓愿。

intro.en: Recluse comes from Late Latin reclusus, 'shut away', built from re- and claudere, 'to close'.
intro.cn: recluse 来自晚期拉丁语 reclusus（被关起来的），由 re- 加 claudere（关闭）构成。

items.en: Claudere meant to close or shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭、合上。

items.en: The compound first meant to open, then to shut someone away.
items.cn: 这个复合词先指打开，后来指把人关起来。

items.en: The participle named a person cut off from the world.
items.cn: 这个分词指与世界隔断的人。

items.en: Recluses were sometimes walled into a cell for life.
items.cn: 中世纪的隐士有时被砌进小屋度过一生。

items.en: Today the word covers anyone who avoids company.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖任何回避人群的人。

definition_zh: 重新造林；在被砍伐或烧毁的林地上恢复森林
definition_en: the act or process of planting trees again on land that has lost its forest cover
core_image: 一片被火烧黑的山坡上，人们沿着等高线把一株株幼苗栽进土里，几年后黑色被树冠盖住
scene: 水库上方那片被山火烧黑的山坡上，村民沿着等高线挖坑栽苗，由政府支付工钱。 A state programme pays villagers to carry out reforestation on the burnt slopes above the reservoir.
sceneCN: 这里 reforestation 指「在失去森林覆盖的土地上重新植树」（第 1 个义项：在被砍伐或烧毁的林地上恢复森林）；句意为一项州政府计划支付工钱，让村民在水库上方被烧黑的山坡上重新造林。图中可辨识物件：黑色树桩、成排幼苗、等高线土埂、水库水面。

senses.title: Plant trees where forest was lost
senses.titleCN: 在被砍伐或烧毁的林地上重新植树
senses.definition: to plant trees again on land whose original forest cover has been removed or destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 在原森林被清除或毁坏的土地上再次栽种树木
senses.example: The county began reforestation of the clear-cut hillside in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 县里在春天开始对那片被皆伐的山坡重新造林。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus forest plus -ation 'process' names the act of putting a forest back where one had been.
senses.whyCN: re-「再次」加 forest 与 -ation「过程」，字面就是「把一个曾有过的森林再放回去」。

senses.title: The programme or process as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为一项工程或过程的重新造林
senses.definition: a organized programme, policy or long process of restoring tree cover over an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一区域恢复树木覆盖的有组织计划、政策或长期过程
senses.example: Reforestation in the watershed has run for twelve years without a break.
senses.exampleCN: 该集水区的重新造林已不间断地进行了十二年。
senses.why: the -ation noun can name not only single planting but the whole institutional effort, which is how governments and NGOs use it.
senses.whyCN: -ation 名词不只指一次栽种，也可指整个制度性行动，政府与环保组织正是这样使用。

senses.title: Restore eroded or degraded land
senses.titleCN: 在退化或侵蚀的土地上恢复植被
senses.definition: to establish tree cover on eroded, salinized or exhausted land in order to hold soil and water
senses.definitionCN: 在受侵蚀、盐渍化或耗竭的土地上建立树木覆盖，以保持水土
senses.example: Reforestation of the gullied slopes cut sediment delivery to the river by half.
senses.exampleCN: 在沟蚀坡地上重新造林，使进入河流的泥沙减少了一半。
senses.why: trees are planted here not for timber but as a physical shield, so the word takes on a soil-conservation reading.
senses.whyCN: 此处栽树不为木材，而是当作物理屏障，因此这个词带上了水土保持的含义。

senses.title: Replant after fire
senses.definition: to replant a burned area, often by hand, before grasses and shrubs close the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在草木封住地表之前，对过火地常以人工方式补植
senses.example: After the crown fire, reforestation crews worked the north slope first.
senses.exampleCN: 树冠火过后，造林队先在北坡作业。
senses.why: fire removes both trees and seed source, so the 'again' in re- is literal: people must supply what the forest cannot regrow on its own.
senses.whyCN: 火灾同时带走树木与种源，所以 re- 的「再次」是字面意义：森林无法自行更新，只能由人补上。

senses.title: Restore the native species mix
senses.definition: to replant with species native to the site so that the original community can reassemble
senses.definitionCN: 用当地原生树种补植，使原有群落得以重新组合
senses.example: Their reforestation mixes oak, hazel and rowan instead of a single conifer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的重新造林混种栎、榛与花楸，而非单一针叶树。
senses.why: modern ecology widened reforestation from 'trees' to 'the right trees', because cover alone does not rebuild a forest.
senses.whyCN: 现代生态学把 reforestation 从「有树」扩展为「种对的树」，因为仅有覆盖并不能重建森林。

senses.title: Planting aimed at carbon uptake
senses.definition: tree planting undertaken mainly to absorb atmospheric carbon and meet climate targets
senses.definitionCN: 主要以吸收大气碳、达成气候目标为目的的植树
senses.example: The utility funds reforestation to offset part of its emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电力公司资助重新造林，以抵消部分排放。
senses.why: once forests were valued as carbon stores, reforestation became a measurable climate instrument rather than only a land-repair act.
senses.whyCN: 当森林被当作碳库计价，重新造林就从单纯的土地修复变成可计量的气候工具。

senses.title: Tree planting inside cities
senses.definition: the planting of trees in urban and peri-urban areas for shade, air and storm-water control
senses.definitionCN: 在城市与城郊栽树，以获得遮阴、净化空气与雨水管理
senses.example: Urban reforestation turned six vacant lots into a shaded green corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 城市造林把六块空地变成一条有树荫的绿色廊道。
senses.why: the word's frame is 'land that lost forest', and paved districts qualify: they too once held trees.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的框架是「失去森林的土地」，铺满水泥的城区同样符合：那里也曾有树。

senses.title: Commercial plantation replanting
senses.titleCN: 商业人工林的重新种植
senses.definition: the replanting of a harvested timber stand with fast-growing trees for later cutting
senses.definitionCN: 在采伐后的林分补种速生树，以备将来再次采伐
senses.example: Company reforestation follows each harvest with a uniform pine seedling.
senses.exampleCN: 公司每次采伐后都用统一的松树苗重新造林。
senses.why: industry keeps the word but narrows it to 'restock the crop', which can conflict with the ecological reading.
senses.whyCN: 林业产业保留这个词，却把它窄化为「补足作物」，这可能与生态义相冲突。

intro.en: Reforestation joins Latin-derived forest with the prefix re- 'again' and the noun suffix -ation; the compound itself is a modern English formation, not a Latin word.
intro.cn: reforestation 由拉丁来源的 forest 加上前缀 re-「再次」与名词后缀 -ation 构成；这个复合词本身是近代英语新造，并非拉丁词。

items.en: Forest goes back to Medieval Latin forestis (silva), 'woodland outside the walls', from foris 'outside, out of doors'. The exact legal origin is still debated.
items.cn: forest 可上溯到中世纪拉丁 forestis（silva）「墙外的林地」，来自 foris「在外面、户外」。其确切的法律来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French forest passed the word into Middle English, where it first named a royal hunting preserve before naming any large wood.
items.cn: 古法语 forest 把这个词带进中古英语，最初指王室猎场，之后才泛指大片树林。

items.en: By the sixteenth century forest meant simply a large area thickly covered with trees, and the verb forest 'to plant with trees' followed.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，forest 已直接指树木茂密的大片土地，动词 forest「植树于」也随之出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century forestry added re- 'again' and -ation 'process' to forest, producing a transparent English compound for replanting after cutting.
items.cn: 19 世纪的林业用语把 re-「再次」与 -ation「过程」加到 forest 上，造出这个结构透明的英语复合词，指采伐后的补植。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first recorded use of reforestation is not securely dated, and whether forestis derives from foris 'outside' or from a Germanic root remains a reconstruction rather than a settled fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：reforestation 的最早书证年代没有可靠定论；forestis 究竟出自 foris「外面」还是日耳曼词根，也只是重构，并非定论。

note.en: Group one collects the -forestation compounds that differ only by prefix; group two collects words for bringing vegetation back.
note.cn: 第一组是只靠前缀区分的 -forestation 复合词；第二组是表示「让植被回来」的近义词。

entries.definition: Ad- 'to' plus forest: planting trees on land that has not recently carried forest, such as bare moor or former farmland.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「朝向」加 forest：在近期没有森林的土地上植树，如光秃荒原或退耕地。

entries.definition: De- 'away, remove' plus forest: clearing trees permanently, the exact reverse of reforestation.
entries.definitionCN: de-「去除」加 forest：永久清除树木，与 reforestation 正好相反。

entries.definition: A British variant that doubles the 'again' idea with re- and ad-; it is largely interchangeable but less common internationally.
entries.definitionCN: 英式变体，用 re- 与 ad- 重复表达「再次」；大体可互换，但国际上较少用。

entries.definition: The bare noun for tree planting without saying whether the land was previously wooded.
entries.definitionCN: 不带前缀的统称，只说植树，不说明该地原本是否有林。

entries.definition: Bringing an entire ecosystem back toward its former structure; reforestation may be only one step in it.
entries.definitionCN: 使整个生态系统回到原有结构；重新造林可能只是其中一步。

entries.definition: Putting plants back into the ground, often in a garden or a small site; it says nothing about a forest.
entries.definitionCN: 把植物重新栽回土里，常用于花园或小块地，并不涉及森林。

entries.definition: Re-establishing any vegetation, including grasses and shrubs, not necessarily trees.
entries.definitionCN: 重建任何植被，包括草与灌木，不一定有树。

entries.definition: Forest renewal from seed or sprouts without planting; reforestation usually implies human planting.
entries.definitionCN: 森林靠种子或萌蘖自行更新；reforestation 通常意味着人工栽植。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + forest + -ation 'process': putting a forest back.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ forest + -ation「过程」：把森林放回去。

normal.en: The family runs forest, reforest, reforestation, afforestation, deforestation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 forest、reforest、reforestation、afforestation、deforestation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reforestation project, large-scale reforestation, reforestation of degraded land.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：重新造林项目、大规模重新造林、退化土地上的重新造林。

normal.en: The prefix re- is the key: afforestation has no 'again', deforestation takes away.
normal.cn: 关键在前缀：afforestation 没有「再次」，deforestation 则是拿走。

normal.en: The figure is a burned slope refilled with seedlings along contour lines.
normal.cn: 意象是被烧黑的山坡上沿等高线补满幼苗。

abstract.en: Think of a page erased and then written over with the same story in a slower hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被擦掉，又用更慢的笔迹把同一个故事重新写上。

abstract.en: Think of a lung regrowing its fine branches after smoke has stripped them.
abstract.cn: 想象肺叶被烟熏掉细枝后，又一点点长回分支。

abstract.en: Think of a debt repaid not in one sum but tree by tree over decades.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债不是一次还清，而是几十年里一棵树一棵树地偿还。

examples.en: Reforestation of the catchment began after the 1998 floods.
examples.cn: 1998 年洪水之后，该集水区开始重新造林。

examples.en: The charity trains farmers in low-cost reforestation.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构培训农民掌握低成本的重新造林方法。

examples.en: Without reforestation, the bare slope will keep sliding into the road.
examples.cn: 若不重新造林，那片裸露坡地会不断塌到路上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ forest（森林）+ ation（动作）」——再把森林种回去 → 重新造林

root: 拉丁 foris「外面」→ 中世纪拉丁 forestis (silva)「墙外林地」→ 古法语 forest → 英语 forest；再加 re-「再次」与 -ation「过程」构成英语新词。forestis 的更深来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one repair: a piece of land has lost its trees, and people put them back, whether the aim is soil, habitat, carbon, shade or timber.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次修补展开：一块土地失去了树，人把树放回去，目的可以是水土、栖息地、碳、遮阴或木材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black burn scar on a hillside being steadily covered by young trees.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡上一道黑色的火烧痕，正被幼树一点点盖住。

branches.en: STARTING POINT: whether the loss came from axes or fire, the first move is to put seedlings in the ground.
branches.cn: 起点：无论失去森林的原因是斧头还是火，第一步都是把苗栽进土里。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: one planting becomes a programme with budgets, crews and years.
branches.cn: 制度化：一次栽种变成有预算、有队伍、跨年份的计划。

branches.en: LAND REPAIR: trees are planted as a shield for soil, water and city air.
branches.cn: 土地修复：树被当作盾牌，护住土壤、水源与城市空气。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL VALUE: the right mix rebuilds a community, and the growing wood stores carbon.
branches.cn: 生态价值：正确的树种组合重建群落，长出的木材储存碳。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: the same act can be narrowed to restocking a timber crop.
branches.cn: 生产：同一个动作也可被窄化为补足木材作物。

intro.en: Reforestation is built from an English noun and two productive affixes, so each piece can be read separately.
intro.cn: reforestation 由一个英语名词与两个能产后缀、前缀构成，各部分是读得出来的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is foris 'outside', which produced forestis; re- and -ation are affixes that English attaches freely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 foris「外面」，它产生 forestis；re- 与 -ation 是英语可自由附加的缀。

items.example: The prefix says the forest is being put back.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀说明森林正被放回去。

items.example: The forest above the village was cut in the 1980s.
items.exampleCN: 村子上方的森林在 1980 年代被砍伐。

items.meaning: the act, process or result of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb reforest into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词 reforest 变成过程之名。

items.example: Crews reforest the slope by hand.
items.exampleCN: 工人以人工方式在这片坡地重新造林。

items.example: Afforestation converted the moor into conifer plantation.
items.exampleCN: 造林把荒原变成了针叶林。

items.example: Deforestation upstream worsened the flooding.
items.exampleCN: 上游的毁林加重了洪水。

items.example: Forestation has no prefix because it picks no starting point.
items.exampleCN: forestation 不带前缀，因为它不指定起点。

items.example: The reforested catchment now holds water longer.
items.exampleCN: 已重新造林的集水区现在能更久地蓄住水。

definition_zh: 污染物；进入环境并造成危害的物质
definition_en: a substance introduced into air, water or soil that damages living things or the uses of that environment
core_image: 清晨的烟囱吐出一股灰白烟柱，顺着风慢慢压低到居民区屋顶的高度
scene: 工厂的排烟口在清晨吐出灰白色烟柱，顺着风散向居民区。 The smokestack released a pollutant that settled over the nearby houses.
sceneCN: 这里 pollutant 指「进入空气并造成危害的物质」（第 2 个义项：排入大气后危害健康或环境的物质）；句意为烟囱排放的一种污染物沉降到附近房屋上空。图中可辨识物件：烟囱、烟柱、风向、居民区屋顶。

senses.title: A substance that damages the environment
senses.titleCN: 对环境造成危害的物质
senses.definition: any substance whose entry into the environment harms organisms, materials or human health
senses.definitionCN: 进入环境后危害生物、材料或人类健康的任何物质
senses.example: The smokestack released a pollutant that settled over the nearby houses.
senses.exampleCN: 烟囱排放的一种污染物沉降到附近房屋上空。
senses.why: Pollutant is pollute plus -ant, so it names the agent that does the polluting rather than the damaged state.
senses.whyCN: pollutant 是 pollute 加 -ant，因此它命名的是「执行污染的那个东西」，而非被污染的状态。

senses.title: An air pollutant
senses.definition: a gas or particle in the air at a level that harms health, visibility or crops
senses.definitionCN: 在空气中达到危害健康、能见度或作物的浓度的气体或颗粒
senses.example: Ground-level ozone is the pollutant that closes the parks in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 近地面臭氧是夏天让公园关闭的那种污染物。
senses.why: Air was the first medium regulated in law, so the word's most familiar sense is the smoke and gas that enters it.
senses.whyCN: 空气是最早被立法管制的介质，因此这个词最熟悉的义项就是进入空气的烟与气体。

senses.title: A water pollutant
senses.definition: a substance in rivers, lakes or groundwater that harms aquatic life or drinking supply
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊或地下水中危害水生生物或饮用水供给的物质
senses.example: Fertiliser runoff is a water pollutant that feeds algal blooms.
senses.exampleCN: 化肥径流是一种水体污染物，会滋养藻华。
senses.why: Water carries substances far from their source, so the word shifted from the pipe to the whole catchment.
senses.whyCN: 水把物质从源头带到很远，这个词于是从管子转向整个流域。

senses.title: A soil pollutant
senses.definition: a substance that accumulates in soil and harms plants, soil life or the food chain
senses.definitionCN: 在土壤中累积、危害植物、土壤生物或食物链的物质
senses.example: Lead was a soil pollutant around every old road.
senses.exampleCN: 铅曾是每条老路周边的一种土壤污染物。
senses.why: Soil holds what water washes out of the air, so the pollutant persists long after the source has gone.
senses.whyCN: 土留住了水从空气中洗下的东西，因此污染源消失很久之后污染仍在。

senses.title: A pollutant that is not a substance
senses.titleCN: 非物质的污染物：噪声、光、热
senses.definition: an excess of noise, light, heat or radiation that degrades the environment without adding matter
senses.definitionCN: 过量的噪声、光、热或辐射，虽不添加物质，却使环境退化
senses.example: Light at night is a pollutant for migrating birds.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间的灯光对迁徙鸟类是一种污染。
senses.why: The word's frame is 'something added that harms', and energy can be added as well as matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的框架是「加了某物而造成危害」，而被加进去的除了物质也可以是能量。

senses.title: A biological pollutant
senses.definition: a pathogen or introduced organism that harms native life or human health
senses.definitionCN: 危害本地生物或人类健康的病原体或外来生物
senses.example: Ballast water carried a biological pollutant across the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 压载水把一种生物污染物带过了大洋。
senses.why: Living invaders follow the same pattern as chemicals: they enter, establish and change the system.
senses.whyCN: 活的入侵者与化学品走同一条路径：进入、立足、改变系统。

senses.title: A substance on a regulatory list
senses.titleCN: 被列入管制清单的物质
senses.definition: a named substance whose concentration in a medium is limited by law or permit
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或许可中被限定于某一介质内浓度的具名物质
senses.example: The permit listed each pollutant and its allowed load.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证列出了每种污染物及其允许排放量。
senses.why: Regulation turns the concept into a list, so pollutant comes to mean a substance that has a legal threshold.
senses.whyCN: 监管把这个概念变成一份清单，pollutant 于是指「有法定阈值的物质」。

senses.title: Abstract: an idea that degrades a field
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：使某个领域变质的东西
senses.definition: a transferred use for information, speech or data that corrupts the quality of a discussion or system
senses.definitionCN: 转指使讨论或系统质量变质的信息、言论或数据
senses.example: Fabricated studies are a pollutant in the literature.
senses.exampleCN: 伪造的研究是文献中的一种污染。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the environmental shape: something enters, spreads and makes the whole medium less fit for use.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了环境形态：某物进入、扩散，使整个介质的可用性下降。

intro.en: Pollutant is formed in English from pollute plus the agent suffix -ant. The verb itself goes back through French to Latin polluere, whose internal history is only partly explained. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pollutant 在英语中由 pollute 加施动后缀 -ant 构成。动词本身经法语可追到拉丁 polluere，其内部构造只得到部分解释。年代均为约数。

items.en: One element of polluere is usually identified as luere 'to wash, to purify'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction, and the connection with lavare 'to wash' is treated as a related form rather than a proved parent.
items.cn: polluere 的一个成分通常被认作 luere「洗、净化」。其更深来源不确定；为它提出的印欧词根是重构，与 lavare「洗」的联系被当作相关形式，而非已证实的母词。

items.en: The verb is analysed as por- (a variant of pro- 'forth') plus luere, but how a washing root produced the sense 'to defile' is not fully explained, and some accounts treat the prefix as merely intensive rather than locative.
items.cn: 这个动词通常被分析为 por-（pro-「向前」的变体）加 luere，但「洗」的词根如何产生「弄脏」之义并未得到完整解释，也有说法把该前缀视为单纯的加强成分而非方位成分。

items.en: Late Latin pollutio named defilement, especially ritual or moral uncleanness, and this religious sense came into English first.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 pollutio 指玷污，尤指仪式或道德上的不洁，这一宗教义最先进入英语。

items.en: English pollute appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of desecrating something sacred; the physical sense of dirtying air or water is much later.
items.cn: 英语 pollute 在十四世纪出现，指亵渎神圣之物；弄脏空气或水的物理义要晚得多。

items.en: From the nineteenth century pollution was applied to smoke, sewage and industrial waste, and pollutant was coined as the countable name for one offending substance.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，pollution 被用于烟、污水与工业废料，pollutant 则作为「一种肇事物质」的可数名称被造出。

items.en: Source uncertain (internal history of polluere and first date of pollutant): the shift from washing to defiling is unexplained, and the noun's earliest technical citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; any older form offered for luere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（polluere 的内部构造与 pollutant 的首见年代）：从「洗」到「弄脏」的转变未获解释，这个名词最早的技术书证也无定论，年代只能约计；凡为 luere 给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same pollute family plus one look-alike with an unrelated root; group two holds other words for harmful inputs, each with a different kind of harm.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 pollute 词族的各种形式，外加一个词根无关的形近词；第二组是其他表示「有害输入」的词，各自的危害方式不同。

entries.definition: The presence or accumulation of pollutants; it names the condition, while pollutant names one substance.
entries.definitionCN: 污染物的存在或累积；它指状态，而 pollutant 指一种物质。

entries.definition: The person or firm that pollutes; it names an actor, not the substance released.
entries.definitionCN: 造成污染的人或企业；它指施动者，而非排放的物质。

entries.definition: To make air, water or soil dirty or harmful; it is the action that produces a pollutant.
entries.definitionCN: 使空气、水或土壤变脏或有害；它是产生污染物的动作。

entries.definition: A head, a survey of votes or a hornless animal, from Middle English polle 'head'; it looks like the poll- of pollute but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 指头、投票调查或无角动物，出自中古英语 polle「头」；它形似 pollute 的 poll-，但并无亲缘。

entries.definition: A substance that makes something impure; it may unfits a product without harming an ecosystem.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不纯的物质；它可能使产品不合格，却未必危害生态。

entries.definition: A poisonous substance; it is defined by toxicity, while a pollutant is defined by environmental harm.
entries.definitionCN: 有毒物质；它以毒性定义，而污染物以环境危害定义。

entries.definition: The act or quantity of something released into the air; it names the outflow, not the substance's harm.
entries.definitionCN: 释放入空气的动作或数量；它指排出流，而非物质的危害性。

entries.definition: Treated or untreated liquid waste flowing out of a plant; it may contain pollutants but is named by its flow.
entries.definitionCN: 从厂区流出的处理过或未处理的废液；它可能含污染物，但以「流」命名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pollutant is pollute plus -ant, the suffix that marks the doer: the substance that does the polluting.
normal.cn: pollutant 是 pollute 加 -ant，这个后缀标出施动者：执行污染的那个物质。

normal.en: The family runs pollute, pollution, polluter, polluted and polluting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pollute、pollution、polluter、polluted 与 polluting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the medium: air pollutant, water pollutant, soil pollutant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出介质：空气污染物、水体污染物、土壤污染物。

normal.en: Regulation turns it into a list: each pollutant has a permitted level or load.
normal.cn: 监管把它变成清单：每种污染物都有允许的浓度或排放量。

normal.en: Poll looks like the same root but means 'head', from Middle English polle.
normal.cn: poll 看似同根，实指「头」，出自中古英语 polle。

abstract.en: Picture smoke entering a valley and staying there because the walls block the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象烟进入一个山谷，因为山壁挡风而留在里面。

abstract.en: Picture one bad number travelling through a chain of reports.
abstract.cn: 想象一个坏数字在一串报告里传下去。

abstract.en: Picture a loud generator that harms nothing you can see but spoils the whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象一台吵闹的发电机，看不见任何损伤，却毁了整条街。

examples.en: The plant must report every pollutant it releases.
examples.cn: 该厂必须报告它排放的每一种污染物。

examples.en: A pollutant may travel hundreds of kilometres before it settles.
examples.cn: 一种污染物可能飘行数百公里才沉降。

examples.en: Noise is treated as a pollutant in the city's zoning code.
examples.cn: 在这座城市的区划法规中，噪声被当作一种污染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pollute（污染）+ ant」——出面把环境弄脏的那一个 → 污染物

root: pollute 加 -ant；pollute 经法语出自拉丁 polluere「弄脏、玷污」，通常分析为 por-（pro- 变体）+ luere「洗」，但由「洗」到「弄脏」的转变未获完整解释，luere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one entry: a substance enters a medium, harms life or use, is listed and limited, may persist, and may even be energy or an idea rather than matter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次进入展开：物质进入某种介质，危害生命或用途，被列入清单并受限额，可能长期留存，甚至可以是能量或一个想法而非物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey plume leaving a stack and sinking onto a row of roofs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股灰烟离开烟囱，压到一排屋顶上。

branches.en: MEDIA: the general definition and the air, water and soil cases differ only in where the substance lands.
branches.cn: 介质：总定义与空气、水、土壤三种情形，区别只在物质落在哪里。

branches.en: ENERGY AS POLLUTANT: noise, light and heat harm by excess rather than by matter.
branches.cn: 能量作污染：噪声、光与热靠过量而非物质造成危害。

branches.en: LIFE AS POLLUTANT: an organism can invade and change a system like a chemical.
branches.cn: 生命作污染：生物也能像化学品一样侵入并改变系统。

branches.en: LAW: a named substance with a threshold is what regulation means by pollutant.
branches.cn: 法律：有名字、有阈值的物质，就是监管所说的污染物。

branches.en: TRANSFER: bad ideas and bad data pollute a medium of thought.
branches.cn: 转移：坏想法与坏数据污染思想的介质。

intro.en: Pollutant is an English derivative of a Latin verb; the suffix is clear, while the internal analysis of the Latin verb is only partly settled.
intro.cn: pollutant 是拉丁动词的英语派生词；后缀清楚，而拉丁动词的内部构造只部分确定。

latinIntro.en: Latin polluere gives pollute, pollution and pollutant; the suffix -ant also forms contaminant, toxicant and coolant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 polluere 衍生 pollute、pollution 与 pollutant；后缀 -ant 也构成 contaminant、toxicant 与 coolant。

items.example: The verb named ritual and physical defilement alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词兼指仪式与物理上的玷污。

items.example: The washing element is the disputed half of polluere.
items.exampleCN: 「洗」这个成分是 polluere 中有争议的一半。

items.example: The suffix marks the substance as the doer.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把该物质标为施动者。

items.example: The mill polluted the river for decades.
items.exampleCN: 这家厂污染河流数十年。

items.example: Air pollution closed the schools.
items.exampleCN: 空气污染使学校停课。

items.example: The list named twelve pollutants.
items.exampleCN: 清单列出了十二种污染物。

items.example: The polluter paid for the cleanup.
items.exampleCN: 污染者支付了清理费用。

items.example: The polluted canal was fenced off.
items.exampleCN: 受污染的运河被围了起来。

items.example: The most polluting cars were banned.
items.exampleCN: 污染最重的汽车被禁行。

items.example: They advertised a pollutant-free process.
items.exampleCN: 他们宣传一种无污染工艺。

definition_en: to move troops or resources into position for action, or to use something effectively
core_image: 指挥图上箭头把几支队伍调到不同位置，服务器机房里新版本被推上线
scene: 公司部署了新的服务器。 The company deployed new servers.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：deployed 指有效利用、投入使用；句意是公司部署了新的服务器。

pos.zh: 部署；调动；有效利用；（计算机）部署，发布

重新部署；调岗

senses.title: Position troops
senses.definition: to move soldiers or equipment into position for action
senses.definitionCN: 把士兵或装备调到可行动的位置
senses.example: The army deployed two brigades along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 军队沿边境部署了两个旅。
senses.why: Arrows on a map moving units into place.
senses.whyCN: 地图上一支支部队被箭头调到位置。

senses.title: Use effectively
senses.definition: to bring resources or skills into effective use
senses.definitionCN: 把资源或技能投入有效使用
senses.example: The company deployed new servers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司部署了新的服务器。
senses.why: A budget line moved to where it works hardest.
senses.whyCN: 一笔预算被挪到最能起作用的地方。

senses.title: Release software
senses.definition: to put a program or system into service on a server
senses.definitionCN: 把程序或系统放到服务器上投入使用
senses.example: They deploy the update every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每周五发布更新。
senses.why: A green light beside a version number.
senses.whyCN: 一个版本号旁边亮起的绿灯。

intro.en: Deploy comes from French déployer, from Latin displicare, dis- plus plicare, to fold: to unfold.
intro.cn: deploy 源自法语 déployer，来自拉丁语 displicare，由 dis- 加 plicare（折叠）构成：展开。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold.
items.cn: plicare 意为折叠。

items.en: Displicare meant to unfold or spread out.
items.cn: displicare 意为展开、铺开。

items.en: Déployer meant to spread out troops.
items.cn: 法语 déployer 指把部队展开。

items.en: Deploy entered English for spreading forces.
items.cn: 十八世纪 deploy 以展开兵力义进入英语。

items.en: It widened to using resources effectively.
items.cn: 二十世纪扩展到有效利用资源。

items.en: Deploy became the word for releasing software.
items.cn: 二十一世纪 deploy 成为发布软件的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ploy- folding family; the near-meaning group names other ways of putting things in place.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ploy-（折叠）家族；近义组是其他「就位」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of deploying troops or software.
entries.definitionCN: 部署。

entries.definition: To spread out for people to see.
entries.definitionCN: 展示。

entries.definition: To use something, or give someone work.
entries.definitionCN: 使用；雇用。

entries.definition: To put something in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 安置。

entries.definition: To put someone in a place for duty.
entries.definitionCN: 驻扎。

entries.definition: To make something available for use.
entries.definitionCN: 发布；释放。

normalIntro.cn: deploy 就是 de-（向外）加 ploy-（折叠）：把折起来的展开，放到能起作用的位置。

normal.en: Ploy- means to fold, as in employ.
normal.cn: ploy- 意为折叠，如 employ。

normal.en: De- here means out.
normal.cn: 这里 de- 表示向外。

normal.en: Deploy troops means spread them out.
normal.cn: deploy troops 指把部队展开。

normal.en: Deploy resources means put them to work.
normal.cn: deploy resources 指把资源投入使用。

normal.en: Deploy the update means put it live.
normal.cn: deploy the update 指把更新上线。

abstract.en: Arrows on a map moving units into place.

examples.en: The team deployed the fix overnight.
examples.cn: 团队连夜部署了修复。

examples.en: They are deploying sensors across the valley.
examples.cn: 他们正在整个山谷布置传感器。

examples.en: She deploys her skills where they matter most.
examples.cn: 她把技能用在最要紧的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: deploy 谐音「弟普洛伊」——不如记 de（展开）＋ ploy（折，与 display 同根 plicare）＝把折起来的铺开，「部署、展开」，软件里就是「发布上线」。

sensesIntro.en: One unfolding: troops on a map, a budget line and a version number.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次展开：地图上的部队、一笔预算与一个版本号。

branches.en: Arrows on a map moving units into place.

definition_zh: 生物学家；研究生命现象的科学工作者
definition_en: a scientist who studies living organisms and the processes of life
core_image: 一个人俯身在显微镜与野外记录本之间，把活的东西写进知识
scene: 他每周从湖里取一次水样，一取就是一整年。 A biologist took water samples from the lake every week for a year.
sceneCN: 这里 biologist 是「生物学家」（第 1 个义项：研究生命现象的科学工作者）；句意：一位生物学家在一年里每周都从湖里取水样。场景要点：湖泊、采样瓶、显微镜、记录本、防水靴。
