senses.title: A scientist of living things
senses.titleCN: 生物学家：研究生命现象的人
senses.definition: a scientist who studies living organisms and life processes
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物与生命过程的科学家
senses.example: A biologist took water samples from the lake every week.
senses.exampleCN: 一位生物学家每周从湖里取水样。
senses.why: bio- is 'life', -logy is 'study', and -ist is 'one who practises'. The suffix makes a person out of a discipline: the biologist is the human face of biology, and the object of study is anything alive.
senses.whyCN: bio- 是“生命”，-logy 是“学科”，-ist 是“从事者”。这个后缀把一门学科变成一个人：生物学家就是生物学的面孔，而研究对象是一切活的东西。

senses.title: The laboratory researcher
senses.titleCN: 实验室生物学家：在台前做实验的人
senses.definition: a biologist who works mainly in a laboratory, using experiments and instruments
senses.definitionCN: 主要在实验室工作、使用实验与仪器的生物学家
senses.example: The biologist spent the morning at the microscope, counting cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生物学家在显微镜前度过了一上午，数细胞。
senses.why: Modern biology is largely experimental, so the default picture of a biologist became a person at a bench. The word names the profession rather than the place, but bench work supplies its most familiar scene.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物学很大程度上是实验性的，所以生物学家的默认形象变成了实验台前的人。这个词命名的是职业而不是地点，但实验台提供了它最熟悉的场景。

senses.title: The field biologist
senses.titleCN: 野外生物学家：在自然中观察的人
senses.definition: a biologist who studies organisms in their natural habitats rather than in a lab
senses.definitionCN: 在自然栖息地而非实验室研究生物的科学家
senses.example: Field biologists camped in the valley to record bird calls at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 野外生物学家在山谷里扎营，记录黎明时的鸟鸣。
senses.why: The other half of the discipline works outdoors. The same title covers both because the object — living things — is the same; only the method and the setting change.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的另一半在户外工作。同一个头衔覆盖两边，因为对象——活的东西——相同，变化的只是方法与场景。

senses.title: A branch specialist
senses.titleCN: 分支生物学家：海洋、分子、细胞等
senses.definition: a biologist identified by the branch of biology they specialize in
senses.definitionCN: 以所专攻的生物学分支来称呼的生物学家
senses.example: A marine biologist explained why the reef was bleaching.
senses.exampleCN: 一位海洋生物学家解释了珊瑚礁为何白化。
senses.why: Biology split into branches, and English simply puts the branch before biologist: marine biologist, molecular biologist. The head noun still marks the person, while the first word narrows the field.
senses.whyCN: 生物学分成许多分支，英语直接把分支放在 biologist 前面：marine biologist、molecular biologist。中心名词仍标记“人”，前面的词则缩小领域。

senses.title: The -ist pattern: practitioner of a discipline
senses.definition: the general pattern by which -ist turns the name of a discipline into the name of the person who practises it
senses.definitionCN: -ist 把学科名称变成从业者名称的一般构词模式
senses.example: Botanists, zoologists and biologists all belong to the same -ist family.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家、动物学家和生物学家都属于同一个 -ist 词族。
senses.why: -ist comes from Greek -istēs, an agent ending. Attaching it to -logy produces 'one who does the study'. The word therefore says what the person practises, not what they are like.
senses.whyCN: -ist 来自希腊语 -istēs，是施事词尾。把它加到 -logy 上就产生“从事这项研究的人”。所以这个词说的是“做什么”，而不是“是什么样的人”。

senses.title: The older sense: a student of life
senses.titleCN: 早期义：研究生命之学的人（1813）
senses.definition: the original English sense: a student of the science of life, with human life especially in view
senses.definitionCN: 英语最早的含义：研究生命之学的人，尤其着眼于人的生命
senses.example: The word biologist was first used in 1813 for a student of the science of life.
senses.exampleCN: biologist 一词在 1813 年最早用来指研究生命之学的人。
senses.why: The earliest English use (1813) still carried the Greek sense of bios as a person's life; the modern professional sense is recorded only by 1859. The word began as 'learner' and later became 'profession'.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的使用（1813）仍带着希腊语 bios“一个人的生命”这层意思；现代职业义直到 1859 年才有记录。这个词从“学习者”开始，后来才成为“职业”。

senses.title: Conservation and applied biologist
senses.titleCN: 保护与应用生物学家：为管理生命而研究
senses.definition: a biologist whose work is directed at protecting or managing species and habitats
senses.definitionCN: 工作指向保护或管理物种与栖息地的生物学家
senses.example: Conservation biologists argue that protecting habitat protects species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护生物学家主张，保护栖息地就是保护物种。
senses.why: When biology is applied to managing species, the title gains a purpose: the biologist is not only describing life but defending it. The compound marks that applied role rather than a new kind of science.
senses.whyCN: 当生物学被用于管理物种时，这个头衔多了一层目的：生物学家不仅在描述生命，也在为生命辩护。这个复合词标记的是应用角色，而不是一门新科学。

senses.title: Biologists as a community
senses.titleCN: 生物学界：作为群体的生物学家
senses.definition: the profession or community of biologists, treated as a body of shared opinion
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个共享观点的群体的生物学家职业共同体
senses.example: Biologists generally agree that the warming ocean is shifting fish stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家普遍认为，海洋变暖正在改变鱼类种群分布。
senses.why: The plural without an article names a profession as a body of opinion. This is the collective sense: not one researcher but the discipline speaking, which is why news reports say 'biologists say'.
senses.whyCN: 不带冠词的复数把一种职业命名为一个观点共同体。这是集体义：说话的不是某位研究者，而是整个学科，所以新闻报道会说 biologists say。

senses.title: Attributive: a biologist's view
senses.definition: used before another noun or after 'as' to name the professional lens through which something is seen
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前或 as 之后，指看待某事物时所采用的生物学家视角
senses.example: As a biologist, she sees the garden as a web of interactions.
senses.exampleCN: 作为生物学家，她把花园看成一个相互作用的网络。
senses.why: Before another noun or after 'as', the word labels the lens through which something is seen. It is still a person, but the person now functions as a viewpoint rather than as the subject of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 置于名词前或 as 之后时，这个词标记的是观察事物所用的镜头。它仍然指人，但此时的人作为“视角”起作用，而不是句子的主体。

intro.en: Biologist is biology + -ist. Biology itself is a modern Greek-Latin hybrid coined around 1800, so the whole family is scientific rather than inherited. The exact first coiner of biology is disputed; the date of biologist is better recorded.
intro.cn: biologist 是 biology + -ist。biology 本身是约 1800 年前后造出的希腊—拉丁混合词，所以整个词族是科学造词而非承袭词。biology 的确切首创者存疑，biologist 的年代记录则较清楚。

items.en: bios means 'life, lifetime, way of life' (PIE *gwei- 'to live'), as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. In modern scientific compounds bio- means 'life, living organisms'.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、寿命、生活方式”（原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”），与 zoē“动物生命”相对。在现代科学复合词里，bio- 表示“生命、生物”。

items.en: logos means 'word, account, reason'. The derived -logia means 'the study of', and English -logy comes through Latin -logia. Biology is therefore 'the account or study of life'.
items.cn: logos 意为“词、叙述、理性”。派生的 -logia 表示“对……的研究”，英语 -logy 经由拉丁语 -logia 而来。因此 biology 就是“关于生命的论述或研究”。

items.en: The compound biology was suggested in 1802 by the German naturalist Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus and introduced in French that same year by Lamarck; the two seem to have hit on it independently. Who first coined it cannot be settled. English biology is recorded in 1819.
items.cn: 复合词 biology 由德国博物学家 Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus 于 1802 年提出，同年由拉马克在法语中引入；两人似乎是独立想到的。谁最先造出这个词无法确定。英语 biology 记录于 1819 年。

items.en: biologist is recorded from 1813, meaning 'a student of the science of life'. The earliest use refers to human life, in the Greek sense of bios; the modern sense 'one skilled in or a student of biology' is recorded by 1859.
items.cn: biologist 自 1813 年有记录，意为“研究生命之学的人”。最早用法指人的生命，取希腊语 bios 之义；现代义“精通或研究生物学的人”到 1859 年才有记录。

items.en: -ist 'one who does or makes' comes from French -iste and Latin -ista, from Greek -istēs, an agent ending built on verb stems. It makes biologist the person who practises what biology names.
items.cn: -ist“从事者”来自法语 -iste、拉丁语 -ista，再往上为希腊语 -istēs——建立在动词词干上的施事前缀。它使 biologist 成为“实践 biology 所示之事的人”。

items.en: Biography is bio- + graphein 'to write', literally 'life-writing', and its person is a biographer. Biology is bio- + -logy 'study', and its person is a biologist. The shared bio- is real, but the second element decides the word: writing versus studying.
items.cn: biography 是 bio- + graphein“书写”，字面“写生命”，其指人名词是 biographer。biology 是 bio- + -logy“研究”，其指人名词是 biologist。共享的 bio- 是真实的，但第二成分决定词义：书写还是研究。

note.en: The first group contains forms built on the same bio- prefix that are easily mistaken for the person; the second contains nearby professions that differ in scope or object.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 bio- 前缀构成、容易被误当成“指人”的形式；第二组是范围或对象不同的邻近职业。

entries.definition: The science of life. It ends in -logy 'study', so it names the field; biologist adds -ist to name the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 生命科学。它以 -logy“研究”结尾，命名的是领域；biologist 加 -ist 才命名从业者。

entries.definition: An account of a person's life, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. Its person is a biographer, never a biologist.
entries.definitionCN: 对一个人生平的记述，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。其指人名词是 biographer，绝不是 biologist。

entries.definition: A rare 19th-century rival for biologist, recorded 1865 and now obsolete. It shows that -ist won the competition.
entries.definitionCN: 19 世纪与 biologist 竞争的罕见说法，1865 年有记录，今已废弃。它说明 -ist 赢下了这场竞争。

entries.definition: Relating to life or living things, from Greek biōtikos. It is an adjective, so it can never name the scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 与生命或生物有关的，来自希腊语 biōtikos。它是形容词，绝不能指科学家。

entries.definition: A researcher in any life science, including biomedicine and biochemistry. Broader than biologist, which usually points to organism-level study.
entries.definitionCN: 任何生命科学领域的研究者，包括生物医学与生物化学。比 biologist 宽，后者通常指生物体层面的研究。

entries.definition: A student of plants and animals through observation, often outside a university. It stresses watching nature rather than running experiments.
entries.definitionCN: 通过观察研究动植物的学者，常在大学之外。它强调观察自然，而不是做实验。

entries.definition: A specialist in animals. It is one branch of biology, so every zoologist is a biologist but not every biologist is a zoologist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究动物的专家。它是生物学的一个分支，所以动物学家都是生物学家，但生物学家不都是动物学家。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies the relations between organisms and their environment. The focus is the system, not the individual organism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境之间关系的科学家。焦点在系统，而不在单个生物体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real branch names, and the real biography contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的分支名称，以及 biography 的真实对比。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + -logy 'study' + -ist 'practitioner': the person who does the study of life.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ -logy“研究”+ -ist“从业者”：从事生命研究的人。

normal.en: Test the ending: -logy is the field, -logist is the person. biology → biologist, geology → geologist.
normal.cn: 看词尾：-logy 是领域，-logist 是人。biology → biologist，geology → geologist。

normal.en: Branch names go before the person: marine, molecular, cell, evolutionary, conservation + biologist.
normal.cn: 分支名放在“人”前面：marine、molecular、cell、evolutionary、conservation + biologist。

normal.en: biography ends in -graphy 'writing', so its person is biographer. Never mix the two second elements.
normal.cn: biography 以 -graphy“书写”结尾，其指人名词是 biographer。不要把两个第二成分混在一起。

normal.en: The word began in 1813 as 'student of life' and only later meant a paid professional; that history explains why it sounds academic.
normal.cn: 这个词 1813 年起初是“研究生命的学生”，后来才指拿薪水的专业人士；这段历史解释了它为何带学术气。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing between a microscope and a muddy boot: lab and field are the two halves of one biologist.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在显微镜和沾泥的靴子之间：实验室与野外是同一个生物学家的两半。

abstract.en: Picture a tree of disciplines: biology is the trunk, and marine, cell, evolutionary biologists are branches bearing the same -ist label.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵学科树：biology 是树干，marine、cell、evolutionary 各支都挂着同一个 -ist 标签。

abstract.en: Picture the suffix as a badge: -ist is pinned on whoever practises the field, so the badge, not the field, makes the person.
abstract.cn: 把后缀想成一枚徽章：谁从事这门领域，-ist 就别在谁身上；造出“人”的是徽章，而不是领域。

examples.en: Biologists still disagree about how many species live in the deep ocean.
examples.cn: 生物学家对深海中有多少物种仍存在分歧。

examples.en: The marine biologist spent three months surveying the coral reef.
examples.cn: 这位海洋生物学家花了三个月调查珊瑚礁。

examples.en: As a biologist, she reads the forest as a set of relationships rather than a collection of trees.
examples.cn: 作为生物学家，她把森林读成一组关系，而不是一堆树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命，欧（o）罗（lo）辑（gi）知识，斯特（st）专门研究 → biologist 生物学家

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ -logia“研究”构成的 biology（约 1802 年新造）+ -ist“从业者”；字面即“研究生命之学的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one person: someone who studies life. What changes is where they work, which branch they name, whether the word means learner or professional, and whether it speaks for one researcher or the whole discipline.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个人：研究生命的人。变化的是工作地点、所属分支、词义是“学习者”还是“职业”，以及说话的是某位研究者还是整个学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who turns living things into knowledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：把活的东西变成知识的人。

branches.en: THE MAKING OF THE WORD: life + study + agent suffix, which is the general -ist pattern.
branches.cn: 词的构成：生命 + 研究 + 施事后缀，也就是 -ist 的一般模式。

branches.en: TWO WORKPLACES: the bench and the field are the two halves of the same profession.
branches.cn: 两个工作场所：实验台与野外是同一职业的两半。

branches.en: SPECIALITY AND PURPOSE: branch names narrow the field, and applied names add a goal.
branches.cn: 分支与目的：分支名缩小领域，应用名增加目标。

branches.en: HISTORICAL LAYER: the earliest sense was 'student of life', not paid professional.
branches.cn: 历史层：最早的义项是“研究生命的学生”，而不是拿薪水的专业人士。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND LENS: the plural can speak for a discipline, and 'as a biologist' names a viewpoint.
branches.cn: 集体与视角：复数可以代表整个学科，as a biologist 则命名一种视角。

intro.en: Biologist is built from three live pieces: bio- (life), -logy (study), -ist (practitioner). Unlike an inherited Latin word, every joint is still visible to a modern reader.
intro.cn: biologist 由三个仍然能产的部分构成：bio-“生命”、-logy“研究”、-ist“从业者”。与承袭的拉丁词不同，每一处接缝对现代读者都仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: The elements come from Greek, not Latin: bios 'life', logos 'account, reason', and -istēs 'one who does'. They entered English through Latin and French forms (-logia, -ista), which is why the endings look Latin even though the roots are Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分来自希腊语而非拉丁语：bios“生命”、logos“叙述、理性”、-istēs“从事者”。它们经由拉丁语和法语形式（-logia、-ista）进入英语，所以词根虽是希腊语，词尾看起来却像拉丁语。

items.example: Biology was her favourite subject at school.
items.exampleCN: 生物学是她上学时最喜欢的科目。

items.example: The biologist recorded the behaviour of the birds.
items.exampleCN: 这位生物学家记录了这些鸟的行为。

items.meaning: relating to biology or living things
items.example: The sample was sent for biological testing.
items.exampleCN: 样本被送去进行生物检测。

items.meaningCN: 从生物学角度；在生物层面
items.example: The two species are biologically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种在生物学上是不同的。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.example: Life is concentrated in the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 生命集中在生物圈内。

items.meaning: a written account of a person's life
items.meaningCN: 传记（bio-“生命”+ -graphy“书写”，第二成分不同）
items.example: She wrote a biography of the chemist.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一部关于这位化学家的传记。

items.meaningCN: 传记作者（与 biologist 的指人后缀不同）
items.example: The biographer interviewed the family.
items.exampleCN: 传记作者采访了这家人。

items.meaning: a scientist who studies rocks and the earth
items.example: A geologist dated the rock layer.
items.exampleCN: 一位地质学家测定了岩层的年代。

items.meaningCN: 动物学家（生物学的一个分支）
items.example: The zoologist studied the migration route.
items.exampleCN: 这位动物学家研究了迁徙路线。

items.example: The botanist identified the plant from its leaves.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家根据叶子辨认出这种植物。

latinEntries.meaning: the study of, an account of
agent ending: one who does or practises
latinEntries.meaningCN: 施事后缀：从事、实践某事的人

definition_zh: 转变；改造；转型；（数学）变换；（生物）转化
definition_en: a thorough change in form, nature or appearance, or the result of such a change
core_image: 同一团黏土在手中被重新塑成完全不同的形状，材质未变而形态全非
scene: 这里指「转变」。 The city underwent a complete transformation after the harbor was rebuilt.
sceneCN: 这里 transformation 指「转变」（第 1 个义项：形态或性质发生根本变化）；句意：港口重建之后，这座城市经历了彻底的转变。图中可辨识物件：新旧街区对照图、起重机、被重新规划的岸线。

pos.zh: 转变；改造；转型；变换；转化（可数，指一次具体变化；也可不可数，指变化过程）

derivatives.zh: 使改变形态；改造；变换
变压器；变形者
有变革作用的；起改造作用的
转换的；变革的（transformational grammar 转换语法）
被改变的；变形后的

senses.title: Radical Change of Form
senses.titleCN: 转变：形态或性质的根本改变
senses.definition: a thorough change in the form or nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物形态或性质发生的彻底变化
senses.example: The city underwent a complete transformation after the harbor was rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 港口重建之后，这座城市经历了彻底的转变。
senses.why: Trans- means 'across' and forma means 'form'. The noun names a crossing from one form to another, and the prefix promises that the distance travelled is large, not a small adjustment.
senses.whyCN: trans- 意为「跨越」，forma 意为「形状」。这个名词命名的是从一种形态跨到另一种形态，而前缀保证跨越的距离很大，不是小修小补。

senses.title: The Changed Result
senses.titleCN: 变化后的形态：转变的产物
senses.definition: the new form that results from such a change
senses.definitionCN: 这种变化所产生的新形态
senses.example: Her final transformation into a singer surprised the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 她最终转变为一名歌手，让全家人都感到意外。
senses.why: The same noun can name either the journey or the place arrived at. Context decides which is meant, and English often uses 'a transformation' for the resulting new state.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既可指旅程，也可指到达之处；语境决定所指，而英语常用 a transformation 来指变化后的新状态。

senses.title: Mathematical Mapping
senses.titleCN: 数学变换：点与点之间的对应
senses.definition: a rule or mapping that carries each point or value to another
senses.definitionCN: 把每个点或数值对应到另一个点或数值的规则
senses.example: A rotation is a transformation that preserves distance.
senses.exampleCN: 旋转是一种保持距离不变的变换。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the word for a change of position or representation that follows a rule. Nothing physical changes; only the coordinates do, which is why the term is so useful.
senses.whyCN: 数学借这个词表示按规则进行的方位或表示方式变化；没有任何实物改变，变的只是坐标——这正是该术语极其有用的原因。

senses.title: Genetic Transformation
senses.titleCN: 遗传转化：细胞接纳外源基因
senses.definition: the introduction of foreign DNA into a cell so that it takes up the new genes
senses.definitionCN: 把外源 DNA 引入细胞，使其接纳新基因
senses.example: The lab used transformation to insert a resistance gene into the bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用转化把一段抗性基因插入细菌。
senses.why: In biology the change is a lasting alteration of the cell's inherited material. The general sense of 'form changed from outside' narrows into 'genome changed from outside'.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学里，变化是对细胞遗传物质的持久改动；「由外部改变形态」的一般含义收窄为「由外部改变基因组」。

senses.title: Syntactic Rewriting
senses.titleCN: 语言学转换：句式的重写
senses.definition: a rule that rewrites one sentence structure into another with the same meaning
senses.definitionCN: 把一种句式改写成另一种同义句式的规则
senses.example: The passive sentence is derived by transformation from the active one.
senses.exampleCN: 被动句由主动句经转换生成。
senses.why: Transformational grammar treats a sentence as passing through rule-governed rewrites. The word is apt because the meaning survives while the shape of the sentence changes.
senses.whyCN: 转换语法把句子看作经过一系列规则化改写；这个词用得很贴切，因为句子的意义保留下来，而句子的外形改变了。

senses.title: Personal Change
senses.titleCN: 人的转变：性情或处境改观
senses.definition: a deep change in a person's character, health or circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格、健康或处境的深刻变化
senses.example: Years of care brought about a slow transformation in him.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的照料使他慢慢发生了转变。
senses.why: The noun is not limited to visible shapes. A person's life can cross from one form to another, and the word then carries hope or moral weight rather than geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词并不限于可见的形状；一个人的生活可以从一种形态跨到另一种，此时该词承载的是希望或道德分量，而不是几何意味。

senses.title: Energy Conversion
senses.titleCN: 能量转换：从一种形式到另一种
senses.definition: the change of energy from one form into another
senses.definitionCN: 能量由一种形式变为另一种形式
senses.example: A turbine converts heat into motion through a series of transformations.
senses.exampleCN: 涡轮通过一连串能量转换把热变成运动。
senses.why: Physics uses the oldest literal sense: the energy is the same quantity but appears in a new form. The prefix trans- is exact here, since the amount is conserved while its dress changes.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用的是最古老的字面义：能量总量不变，只是以新形式出现；这里 trans- 非常准确，因为总量守恒，改变的只是它的「外衣」。

senses.title: Structural Overhaul
senses.titleCN: 结构性改造：体制或产业重构
senses.definition: a far-reaching reorganization of an institution, economy or system
senses.definitionCN: 机构、经济或体制的深远重组
senses.example: The transformation of the postal service took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 邮政系统的改造用了十年。
senses.why: When the object is an organization, the change is in its structure rather than its surface. The word then belongs to policy and management talk, where it signals depth and scale.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是组织机构时，改变的是结构而非表面；此时该词属于政策与管理话语，标出的是深度与规模。

intro.en: Transformation comes from Late Latin transformatio, built on the verb transformare, itself trans- 'across' plus forma 'form'. It reached English through Old French, so the exact first date is approximate.
intro.cn: transformation 出自晚期拉丁 transformatio，它建立在动词 transformare 之上，而 transformare 即 trans-「跨越」加 forma「形状」。该词经古法语进入英语，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Latin forma named a shape, a mould and, by extension, a pattern or beauty. Its family reaches English in form, formal, format, formula, uniform and reform.
items.cn: 拉丁 forma 指形状、模子，并引申指样式或美。其词族以 form、formal、format、formula、uniform、reform 等进入英语。

items.en: Transformare joined trans- 'across' to formare 'to shape', giving 'to shape across, to change the form of'. Classical Latin used it for changing appearance as well as for metamorphosis.
items.cn: transformare 把 trans-「跨越」与 formare「塑造」结合，意为「跨形塑造、改变形状」。古典拉丁既用它指改变外观，也指变形。

items.en: The action noun transformatio named the act of changing form. The -tio suffix marks a completed act viewed as a thing, which is why English -ation nouns so often feel like events.
items.cn: 动作名词 transformatio 指改变形状的行为。-tio 后缀把完成的动作当作一个事物来看，因此英语 -ation 名词常带有「事件」的质感。

items.en: Transformation entered English around the fourteenth century through Old French transformation. Early uses were mostly religious, for a change of the soul or the body.
items.cn: transformation 约于十四世纪经古法语 transformation 进入英语；早期用法多属宗教语境，指灵魂或身体的改变。

items.en: Mathematics, physics and biology later borrowed the word for rule-bound changes of coordinates, of energy form and of genetic material. The core idea stayed the same: one form crosses into another.
items.cn: 数学、物理学与生物学后来借这个词表示受规则约束的坐标变化、能量形式变化与遗传物质变化；核心观念未变：一种形态跨越到另一种形态。

note.en: The first group separates forms built on the same Latin root or on a neighbouring concept. The second holds near-synonyms that differ in scale, speed or type of change.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁词根、或概念相邻的形态；第二组是变化规模、速度或类型不同的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to change the form of'. It names the doing, while transformation names the deed or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为「改变……的形态」；它表示做的动作，而 transformation 表示这一行为或其结果。

entries.definition: The process of passing from one state to another. It stresses the interval, whereas transformation stresses how different the end state is.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指从一种状态转到另一种状态的过程；它强调中间那段间隔，而 transformation 强调终态差异之大。

entries.definition: A change of one substance or element into another, historically linked to alchemy. It is narrower and more dramatic than transformation.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种物质或元素变成另一种，历史上与炼金术相关；比 transformation 更狭窄、更具戏剧性。

entries.definition: Any difference from a previous state. It says nothing about depth, so it can describe a swapped label or a remade city.
entries.definitionCN: 任何与先前状态的差异；不涉及深度，因此既可指换了一个标签，也可指重建一座城市。

entries.definition: A change from one use, purpose or system to another, as a barn converted into a house. It stresses function rather than shape.
entries.definitionCN: 从一种用途、目的或制度转为另一种，如谷仓改作住宅；强调功能而非形状。

entries.definition: A complete change of form, especially in an animal's development. It is more vivid and more specific than transformation.
entries.definitionCN: 形态的彻底改变，尤指动物发育过程；比 transformation 更生动、更具体。

entries.definition: A thorough examination and repair of a system or machine. It implies restoring fitness rather than becoming something new.
entries.definitionCN: 对系统或机器的彻底检查与修理；暗示恢复良好状态，而不是变成新事物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trans- 'across' + forma 'form' + -ation: a crossing from one shape to another.
normal.cn: trans-「跨越」+ forma「形状」+ -ation：从一种形状跨到另一种形状。

normal.en: The family runs transform, transformation, transformer, transformative, transformational, form, format, formula.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 transform、transformation、transformer、transformative、transformational、form、format、formula。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the domains: digital transformation, economic transformation, genetic transformation, energy transformation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：数字化转型、经济转型、遗传转化、能量转换。

normal.en: transition is the passage; transformation is the difference between the ends.
normal.cn: transition 是过程，transformation 是两端之间的差异。

normal.en: A transformer in the street changes voltage, a literal child of this family.
normal.cn: 街上的变压器改变电压，正是这个词族的字面后代。

abstract.en: Picture a caterpillar dissolving inside a shell and a winged thing climbing out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毛虫在壳内溶解，一个有翅的东西爬出来。

abstract.en: Picture the same lump of clay becoming a bowl, then a cup, then a bird.
abstract.cn: 想象同一团黏土先变成碗，再变成杯，再变成一只鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a street that looks the same on the map but is unrecognizable from the pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街在地图上没变，站在人行道上却已认不出来。

examples.en: The transformation of the old mill into a museum took three years.
examples.cn: 把旧磨坊改造成博物馆花了三年。

examples.en: Energy transformation always leaves some heat behind.
examples.cn: 能量转换总会留下一些热。

examples.en: His transformation from clerk to mayor surprised no one who knew him.
examples.cn: 他从职员变成市长，认识他的人都不觉得意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: trans（跨越）+ form（形状）+ ation（名词词尾）→ 跨过原有形状 → 转变、改造

root: 拉丁 trans-「跨越」+ forma「形状、模子」→ transformare「改变形状」→ 晚期拉丁 transformatio → 古法语 transformation → 英语 transformation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share the picture of crossing from one form to another, applied to an object, a result, a mathematical rule, a cell, a sentence, a person, energy and an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一幅画面——从一种形态跨到另一种形态——只是施加于对象、结果、数学规则、细胞、句子、人、能量与机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same clay reshaped into a different figure, material unchanged.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一团黏土被重新塑成另一个样子，材质未变。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY AND THE ARRIVAL: one noun names both the act of changing and the new form that results.
branches.cn: 旅程与抵达：同一个名词既指变化的行为，也指变化所产生的新形态。

branches.en: RULE-GOVERNED REWRITING: points and sentences are carried to new positions or shapes while relations are preserved.
branches.cn: 受规则约束的改写：点与句子被带到新位置或新外形，而关系保持不变。

branches.en: MATERIAL FROM OUTSIDE: a cell takes in foreign genes, so the change enters the inherited substance itself.
branches.cn: 外来物质：细胞接纳外源基因，变化深入到遗传物质本身。

branches.en: INNER AND INSTITUTIONAL: a person or an organization crosses into a new state, and the word gains moral or political weight.
branches.cn: 个人与机构：人或组织跨入新状态，该词由此获得道德或政治分量。

branches.en: CONSERVED QUANTITY: energy changes dress but not amount, the most literal use of trans-.
branches.cn: 守恒的量：能量换了外衣却不改总量，这是 trans- 最字面的用法。

intro.en: Transformation is a Latin action noun: a prefix of crossing, the root for form, a verb-forming suffix and a noun ending that turns the act into a thing.
intro.cn: transformation 是拉丁动作名词：表示跨越的前缀、表示形状的词根、构成动词的后缀，以及把行为变成事物的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma supplies form, formal, format, formula, uniform and reform; transformare adds the crossing prefix and supplies transform, transformation, transformer and transformative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma 衍生 form、formal、format、formula、uniform、reform；transformare 加上跨越前缀，衍生 transform、transformation、transformer、transformative。

items.meaning: the act or result of changing form
items.meaningCN: 改变形态的行为或结果
items.example: The transformation left the outer walls intact.
items.exampleCN: 这次改造保留了外墙。

items.example: New irrigation transformed the valley.
items.exampleCN: 新的灌溉改变了山谷的面貌。

items.meaning: a device or person that transforms
items.example: The transformer stepped the voltage down.
items.exampleCN: 变压器把电压降了下来。

items.meaning: having the power to change something deeply
items.example: The trip was a transformative experience.
items.exampleCN: 那次旅行是一次具有改变作用的经历。

items.example: Transformational grammar rewrites deep structures.
items.exampleCN: 转换语法改写深层结构。

items.example: Water takes the form of its container.
items.exampleCN: 水会呈现容器的形状。

items.example: The walls were painted a uniform grey.
items.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成统一的灰色。

items.meaning: to shape again, usually for improvement
items.example: The law was reformed in 1998.
items.exampleCN: 该法律于 1998 年得到改革。

intro.en: Bereft is the irregular past participle of bereave, from Old English bereafian.
intro.cn: bereft 是 bereave 的不规则过去分词，源自古英语 bereafian。

items.en: the root reup- or reub- meant to snatch, to plunder.
items.cn: 词根 reup- 或 reub- 意为「抢夺」（重构形式）。

items.en: berefte served as past and participle alongside bereaved.
items.cn: 中古英语 berefte 与 bereaved 并存，作过去式和分词。

items.en: bereft became standard for the participle and grew adjective uses.
items.cn: 十七世纪 bereft 成为标准分词形式，并发展出形容词用法。

items.en: it now lives mostly as an adjective of loss and emptiness.

entries.definitionCN: 围城营地；同盟者——beleaguer 的基础词

entries.definition: an alliance of members
entries.definitionCN: 同盟——与 leaguer 同源的普通名词

entries.definition: to surround with armed forces
entries.definitionCN: 围攻——同用 be- 前缀的近义词

entries.definition: to surround militarily or press with questions
entries.definitionCN: 围攻；也指人被纠缠围问

entries.definition: to persistently harass
entries.definitionCN: 不断袭扰；强调反复性

entries.definition: to arrange for battle, or to fortify
entries.definitionCN: 布阵；设防——共享战争语义场

normalIntro.en: Beleaguer is be- plus leaguer: camp round a place.
normalIntro.cn: beleaguer 是 be- 加 leaguer：在某地四周扎营。

normal.en: A beleaguered city is surrounded by an army.
normal.cn: beleaguered city 指被军队围困的城市。

normal.en: The Dutch root leger means camp.
normal.cn: 荷兰语词根 leger 意为「营地」。

normal.en: League comes from the same Germanic root.
normal.cn: league 与之同源（同一日耳曼词根）。

normal.en: Beleaguered by criticism is a common figurative use.
normal.cn: beleaguered by criticism 是常见的比喻用法。

normal.en: Besiege is the plain near-synonym.
normal.cn: besiege 是直接的近义词。

abstract.en: See watchfires ring a city wall by night.
abstract.cn: 看夜里环城而起的篝火。

abstract.en: Feel bread run short and hope run shorter.
abstract.cn: 感受面包渐少、希望更少。

abstract.en: Picture troubles pitching tents round one tired face.
abstract.cn: 想象难题在一个疲惫的脸旁扎下营帐。

examples.en: Rebel forces had beleaguered the capital for months.
examples.cn: 叛军围困首都已经数月。

examples.en: The scandal left the minister beleaguered on every front.
examples.cn: 丑闻让部长在各条战线上都焦头烂额。

examples.en: The beleaguered garrison held out until relief came.
examples.cn: 被围的守军坚持到了援军到来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比·离隔」——敌人把城围得比隔离墙还严实，正是「围困」。

root: 前缀 be-（荷兰语动词化前缀）加 leger（荷兰语「营地、床铺」，与英语 league 同出日耳曼词根，指「联合扎营」）；荷兰语 belegeren「环营围困」于十六世纪经战事进入英语，十七世纪引申出「为困境所困」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: One verb camps armies round a city and troubles round a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词，既让军队环城扎营，也让难题绕人不去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: watchfires encircling a walled city at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里环绕城墙的连绵营火。

intro.cn: beleaguer 保留荷兰语动词形态：be- 加 leger。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the root is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词根属日耳曼语源。
